articleTitle: A Study of Post Process Wafer-Less Chamber Clean Recipe in Lele Process
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Study of post process chamber plasm clean in ICP (inductive coupling plasma) chamber has attracted more interest in past decades for by-product peeling defect and first-wafer issue in sub-28nm process. Insufficient post process clean will induce memory effect and impact 1st processed wafer critical dimension (CD). Moreover, rudimental by-product will accumulate on chamber wall and induce peeling defect during process. However, over-clean is another drawback in post clean. Coating layer on ICP chamber, mostly Y2O3, will be damaged by plasma and induce coating peeling in high RF hours. In our paper, in order to balance cleaning efficiency and chamber coating damage, a series of experiments are taken, and optical emission spectrum analysis is applied to evaluate wafer-less auto clean recipe (WAC). As a result, an effective WAC recipe is proposed and inline CD trend and defect performance are considered. Besides, cleaning mechanism of CIP WAC recipe is also investigated in this paper.

articleTitle: Perspective on Plasma Etching in Advanced Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Advanced packaging is the growth engine of the semiconductor industry. In this work, we summarized the current progress of the plasma etching technology used in the advanced packaging, such as through silicon vias (TSV), silicon cavity etching, plasma dicing, wafer thinning, and descum. The 3D TSV is getting to have smaller critical dimension (CD) to maintain Moore's Law. Silicon wafer with less warpage can replace the organic carrier in fan-out wafer level packaging. Plasma dicing will be treated with smaller CD to fulfill the requirement of advanced process. Wafer thinning moves towards higher uniformity and higher etch rate in plasma etching. Descum has several functionalities required in the advanced packaging, which are surface activation, surface cleaning, and photoresist (PR)/polyimide (PI) striping/ashing. Looking into the future, plasma etching is still a key process for the advanced packaging.

articleTitle: A Transient Enhanced Output Capacitor-Less LDO With Adaptive Biasing and Spike Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, a transient enhanced output capacitor-less low dropout regulator (LDO) is proposed with adaptive biasing technique and spike reduction circuits. The presented adaptive biasing circuit with differential flip voltage followers (DFVFs) can reduce transient spikes and recovery time significantly without consuming large quiescent current. The main part of spike reduction circuits includes two hysteresis comparators with charging and discharging transistors. Simulation results show that during a transient load current step from 0 to 10mA within 100 ns, the overshoot and undershoot spike can be decreased to less than 50mV with a 20pF output capacitor CL. The total current consumption of the proposed LDO is 7uA. The LDO is designed in a 40 nm CMOS technology, and simulation results show its excellent figure-of-merit (FOM).

articleTitle: A Hardware Accelerator of the Convolutional Spike Neural Network Based on STDP Online Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) excel in object recognition but are computationally intensive and unsuitable for online learning. Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup> have low computational requirements, fast processing, and low power consumption, making them suitable for online learning. This paper proposes a hardware accelerator for a Convolutional Spiking Neural Networks (Conv-SNNs) which combines the strengths of CNNs and SNNs by introducing spiking mechanisms into the convolutional layers. It utilizes Spike Timing Dependent Plasticity (STDP) and Reward-STDP (R-STDP) algorithms for training, achieving 95% accuracy on MNIST dataset. In addition, it also supports the few-shot learning. Implemented on Xilinx's ZCU102 FPGA at a 100MHz clock frequency, the system achieves 0.16s for inference and 0.177s for training per image, 16x faster than CPU. The power consumption is 3.979W, two orders of magnitude lower than CPU.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of Polarization Switching Speed in Ferroelectric HfO2 for High-Speed and Low-Power Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this work, the HZO-based ferroelectric (FE) polarization switching speed is experimentally and systematically investigated considering device structure and fabrication process. The mechanisms of FE switching speed dependence are further analyzed, and the effect on nucleation process during switching is found to be the dominant factor. Furthermore, design guidance for high-speed low-power FE devices on device structure and annealing condition is proposed based on the discussion, paving the way for the design of high-performance FE devices and circuits.

articleTitle: Ion Beam Shaping as a Solution for Ultra-High Precision Planarization Process
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an ultra-high precision planarization process based on ion beam shaping (IBS) to meet the stricter requirements of current advanced process technology node miniaturization and chip 3D development process. Under this high stability process, nanoscale or angstrom level thickness and uniformity control across whole wafer can be achieved. We have recently demonstrated atomic level ultra precision modification capability via ion beam shaping (IBS) technology in multiple scenarios. Some examples include: surface roughness modification, CMP-like polishing, etch back process and loading improvement. Which ultimately achieving 3σ < 15Å within 300mm wafers, meeting the strict intra wafer uniformity goals for Fin-FET or even GAA technology.

articleTitle: A Common Framework Solution for Firmware Test on V93000 ATE Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: With the development of semiconductors industry. Screening and characterization test of high-performance chips on ATE (Automatic Test Equipment) are facing much more challenges. In order to improve test coverage and efficiency, more and more IPs are being tested on ATE using firmware test. This paper provides a common framework solution for V93000 to implement firmware test. At the same time, an innovation HTOL (high-temperature operation life test) and CHAR (characterization) test framework is introduced in this paper.

articleTitle: Stochastic Computing Hardware Design and Optimization for Convolutional Neutral Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: With the great advancements in wearable devices and Internet of Things (IoTs), there is a growing interest in implementing Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) in embedded and portable systems. However, the incorporation of artificial intelligence (AI) characteristics into mobile IoT devices results in power and area consumption issues. Currently, Stochastic Computing (SC) demonstrates great promise in enabling highly scalable and extremely low hardware footprint implementations of CNNs. By utilizing AND gates and multiplexers to perform multiplications and additions, SC can achieve significant reductions in power consumption and hardware footprint compared to traditional binary arithmetic implementations. This energy-efficient and hardware-saving computation makes it more feasible to deploy deep learning models on mobile devices. In this paper, an efficient bipolar SC architecture for CNN is designed to optimize these issues. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms traditional binary logic and other SC implementations in terms of hardware resources and energy consumption while maintaining good accuracy.

articleTitle: Ultra Low Temperature High Aspect Ratio Oxide Punch Through Etching
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: BCD (Bipolar - CMOS - DMOS) <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]–[5]</sup> products have been widely used as power management chips. Oxide punch through etching is an important process in the BCD flow, directly affecting silicon deposition, thereby affecting the grounding of the substrate. This layer requires a high Oxide / Silicon selectivity to prevent Silicon recess, as well as minimal consumption of the oxide liner for sidewall to prevent poly gap fill from generating void. This paper introduces an ultra-low temperature oxide etching method. Although the aspect ratio exceeds 4X:1, the sidewalls of the oxide liner are almost not consumed, and a high Oxide / Silicon selection ratio greater than 10X is achieved, perfectly meeting the requirements.

articleTitle: Design of Large-Scale Power Battery Safety Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This paper proposes a safety monitoring system for large-scale power batteries. The system is based on a Central Control Unit and a Safety Monitoring Unit. It can automatically collect important parameters such as voltage, current, temperature, and insulation resistance during the charging and discharging process of the power batteries. The relevant data of the battery pack can be uploaded to the server through Ethernet, realizing the monitoring of the power battery parameters and real-time fault diagnosis to improve the safety of the battery system. In addition, the Central Control Unit can communicate bidirectionally with the Safety Monitoring Unit through the CAN FD bus to control the charging and discharging working status of the battery pack. The test results of this paper show that the CAN FD bus can achieve high-speed data interaction within a communication distance of 15 meters. The insulation resistance monitoring accuracy of the Safety Monitoring Unit can reach 2%, and the voltage measurement accuracy is ±5mV, while the current measurement accuracy is 1%.

articleTitle: Ultra-Short Channel Polymer Transistors
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Shortening the channel length is of significant importance for studying the charge carrier transport in polymer semiconductors. Due to the poor compatibility, polymer semiconductor thin films may be damaged during the photolithography process, affecting device performance. Consequently, reducing the channel length of polymer transistors presents a formidable challenge. In this work, we utilized an aluminum (Al) self-oxidation approach to fabricate polymer transistors with a channel length of approximately 10 nm, obviating the requirement for photolithography processes. Furthermore, a quantitative analysis of the device was performed, revealing an ultrashort-channel transistor with a negligible Schottky barrier. This work provides a convenient platform for studying polymer transport.

articleTitle: Side-Wall Angle Uniformity Improvement in Shallow Trench Isolation Process
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In shallow trench isolation (STI) process, side-wall angle is an important parameter to achieve high quality isolation silicon oxide filling. Here, HBr, and O2 are utilized as the main etch gases to etch silicon in STI by inductively coupled plasma etcher, with a much side-wall angle center/edge difference. To deal with the situation, two methods are studied: adding dilute gas, and optimizing electrical static chuck temperature. Both of them are effective to improve side-wall angle uniformity, which enhances the yield of STI process in wafer fabrication.

articleTitle: Producer-GT ™ High Productivity CCP ETCH Solution
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Producer-GT ™ is designed for dielectric capacitively coupled plasma (CCP) etch applications with great throughput. It offers not only the productivity advantages of dual wafer handling and processing, but also cost effectiveness of parts simplification and corrosion resistance. The Producer-GT ™ etch system can support up to six wafer processing environments, two per twin chamber, achieving high productivity etch process.

articleTitle: Challenge of Boron-Doped Silicon Hard Mask Removal
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, we studied the etching of boron-doped silicon using etching gases such as Cl2/HBr, and finally stopped it on the SiN film layer (SiN loss<10nm), focusing on solving the problems of polymer on the SiB surface and SiN sidewall during the etching process, as well as insufficient SiB/SiN selection ratio. During the process, we found that adding an appropriate amount of O2 to Cl2 and HBr can improve the selectivity of SiB to SiN. In addition, using pulse mode etching or reducing pressure within an appropriate range, increasing bass power, and adjusting O2 content can effectively remove the presence of polymers on the SiB surface and SiN sidewalls. This can be applied to other boron doped silicon etching processes that require high selectivity.

articleTitle: Metal-Oxide-Metal Capacitor Simulation and Modeling by Virtual Fabrication
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this study, a Metal-Oxide-Metal capacitor is fabricated, calibrated, and modeled in a virtual fabrication platform. The capacitance performance is evaluated using different numbers of metal layers, metal fingers, and metal to metal space through execution of a full factorial DOE. A traditional compact model and a neural network model are used to fit the simulation data, respectively. The neural network model displayed a 0.81% fitting error, which was superior to that obtained with the compact model.

articleTitle: Investigation of Amorphous Silicon as Dry Etch Hard Mask in BEOL Low-k Dielectric Patterning
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In order to better adapt to ever-evolving manufacturing processes and improve critical dimension (CD) control in CMOS Back End of Line (BEOL), an investigation using amorphous silicon (a-Si) as the dry etch hard mask in low-k dielectric patterning is performed, which targets for a higher selectivity toward low-k dielectric than the conventional metal hard mask.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Investigation of Insufficient IMC in SOIC Through Advanced Statistical Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In the context of copper ball bonding in semiconductor packaging, an insufficient IMC implies an inadequate intermetallic connection between the aluminum bond pad and the copper ball. This deficiency introduces the potential risk of ball lift issue, thereby adversely affecting the product's reliability performance. The impacted package type is the Small Outline Integrated Circuit (SOIC), primarily employed in automotive applications. It is imperative that the IMC meets compliance standards immediately upon assembly (0 hours), rendering non-compliance unacceptable. Consequently, ensuring a compliant IMC is imperative during the project development phase. This paper delves into the multifaceted factors contributing to insufficient IMC occurrences, with a particular focus on the role of wire bonder Machine-to-Machine (MTM) variation during the wire bonding process. Furthermore, it outlines strategies for addressing this issue, encompassing measures such as precise MTM calibration to achieve stable and dependable output responses.

articleTitle: Dishing Study on Chemical Mechanical Planarization (CMP)
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Dishing as the unavoidable side effect in the process of CMP has an important impact on the wafer loading and process window. Dishing always comes from the high selective ratio of slurry. The paper [1] [2] presented the dishing theoretical model and the influence factor, and offered the direction for the improvement of dishing in CMP. Furthermore, the experiment in the paper shows that the surrounding and location of monitor pad designed for dishing characterization also play an important role in dishing quantification.

articleTitle: Jitter Reduction for Multi-GHZ ATE Up to 20 GHZ
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This paper describes methods for reducing random jitter (RJ) of clock signals in multi-GHz automated test equipment (ATE). The methods are based on real-time averaging of parallel/synchronized signals with largely uncorrelated RJ. Prior work (up to 10 GHz) is extended by demonstrating applicability to frequencies up to 20 GHz with resulting RJ less than 200 femtoseconds (fs). The theory of operation is reviewed and experimental results are shown for 10, 12, 18, and 20 GHz. A de-embedding procedure is used to separate the jitter contribution of the test instruments (jitter “floor”) from the measured values to obtain a close estimation of the actual ultra-low jitter values of the measured signals.

articleTitle: Flattening the Silicon Nitride Surface of Semiconductor Chips Through Etching Processes
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: After multiple cycles of thin film deposition in the chip manufacturing process, steps will naturally occur, causing local or global protrusions and unevenness on the chip surface. This article introduces the phenomenon of local or global protrusions and unevenness on the wafer surface after deposition of silicon nitride thin films. The CF gas containing H and high argon gas volume flow rate are flattened under strong physical bombardment conditions using plasma plasma etching technology, and the silicon nitride thin film will stop at the designated position through a high selectivity etching process of silicon nitride on silicon dioxide.

articleTitle: High-Resolution Time Domain Reflectometry in Advanced Package Failure Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: With the rapid development of advanced packaging, various 2.5D and 3D packaging methods have emerged, including SiP, CoWoS, TSV, PoP and more. The failure in wiring and bonding structures of advanced packaging is detectable at a precision level of less than a hundred micrometer. To address open and short failures in advanced packages, high-resolution Time Domain Reflectometry has been implemented. This technique utilizes laser technology to generate high-frequency Terahertz pulses, enabling a thorough analysis of failure locations with a remarkable <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> resolution.

articleTitle: A Study of the Via Pattern Lithography Process Window Under the 7 NM Logic Design Rules With 193 NM Immersion Lithography
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The rapid advancement of integrated circuit technology has imposed increasingly stringent process constraints within photolithography, driven by the escalating requirements for higher integration levels in chip manufacturing. Due to the two-dimensional nature of vias, their minimum pitch exceeds that of metals, resulting in complex mask decomposition. Therefore, understanding the size constraints of typical via patterns in a single exposure becomes crucial, for simplifying the exposure process of the via layer and reducing manufacturing costs. In this paper, we discuss several patterns under 7 nm logic design rules with a Minimum Metal Pitch (MMP) of 40 nm. The simulation results suggest that when the pitch is 113 nm, the process window nears the recommended value necessary for actual photolithography processes. Additionally, for larger pitch via patterns, manufacturing requirements can still be met.

articleTitle: Optimization and Validation of Sampling and TD-GCMS Analysis for Volatile Organic Compounds from Semiconductor Cleaning Coupons
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Volatile organic contamination (VOC) may deposit on the surfaces of wafers and damage final products. A good cleaning process can minimize the presence of VOCs in the manufacturing parts after a long-term usage. This study describes the optimization of a micro-chamber (µ-chamber)-based extraction method coupled with a thermal desorption - gas chromatography/mass spectroscopy (TD-GCMS) analysis. Next, the optimized sampling and analytical methods were validated by using a standard mixture of hydrocarbons, which proved the validity of the developed methods. Finally, the proposed method was successfully applied for the quantification of VOCs in real washed coupons, demonstrating its capability for the evaluation of VOC emissions in semiconductor cleaning processes.

articleTitle: Feasibility Analysis of Skip ILD CMP Scheme on 28nm Technology Node
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Scratches from ILD CMP (Inter-layer Dielectric Chemical Mechanical Planarization) process directly affect the yield and reliability of devices, which is increasingly serious as the design rule shrinks. Out of the purpose of cost-reduction and yield-improvement, we propose a novel scheme of skipping ILD CMP on 28nm technology node. In this work, feasibility of Skip ILD CMP scheme has been verified by ADI (After Development Inspection) data, AEI (After Etch Inspection) data, oxide profiles, defects. The experimental results showed the acceptable variation of CD and CDU after lithography and etch, both excellent local and global planarization of oxide surfaces were achieved by CTW CMP, and the scratches were effectively avoided.

articleTitle: Investigation on the Root Cause of ESD Failure of Large Size WBBGA Package Chip
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, the root causes of electrostatic discharge (ESD) problems in large size wire bonding ball grid array (WBBGA) package chips are investigated, and two aspects of failure are confirmed. One is related to the test process. The 1-V curve test process is not standardized, resulting in damage to the internal circuit function of the chip. The second is related to design defects. The open/short (O/S) failure is caused by the weak connection point at the pad, and the leakage failure is caused by the insufficient number of power clamps. Hot spot localization analysis provides favorable evidence. The results of this paper provide guidance for the modification and strengthening of ESD protection design, and standardize the ESD testing process, effectively avoiding the recurrence of such ESD failures.

articleTitle: A Novel Hybrid-Channel Gate-All-Around Nanosheet Transistor for Leakage Control and Subthreshold Slope Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: We report a novel Hybrid-channel Gate-AlI-Around (GAA) nanosheet field-effect transistor (NSFET) for the first time. By introducing a reverse biased p-i-n sub-channel, the proposed Hybrid-channel NSFET is able to combine the advantages of GAA MOS channel and sub-TFET channel, achieving superior sub-channel leakage control and possible sub-60m V /dec subthreshold slope (SS), thus significantly alleviating the critical issues of parasitic channel leakage and degraded SS in conventional NSFETs. Simulated Hybrid-channel NSFET exhibits comparable leakage current level with NSFET based on Full BDI scheme, yet with excellent immunity to process variations at the same time. A steep minimum SS of 11.38 mV/dec and average SS of 36.67 mV/dec for 6 decades have also been obtained through bandgap engineering of the sub-TFET channel.

articleTitle: Chemical Effect Mechanism in Chemical Mechanical Polishing of Silicon Wafer
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, the effect of the addition of three additives (A1, A2, and A3) to the polishing slurry on the surface of single crystal silicon during chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) is compared. It is found that A3 has better hydrophilicity by atomic force microscopy (AFM) and contact angle experiments, and its mechanism was analyzed.

articleTitle: ILD-CMP Wafer Edge Thickness Profile Stability Improvement via Acid Silicon Oxide Slurry Formulation Design
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Acid silicon oxide slurry has many advantages in practical applications due to its low solid content, which provides good defect performance, better planarization efficiency, low cost and so on compared with traditional alkaline silicon oxide slurry. So far, it is being widely used in fab ILD CMP process all over the world. Since its low solid content, which is ∼70% less than that of alkaline silicon oxide slurry, the wafer edge (radius was 125mm∼150mm) thickness profile stability is difficult to control in ILD CMP process. ILD CMP post thickness profile is a key production index in the fab. In this research, the ILD CMP wafer edge profile stability was studied via adjusting acid silicon oxide slurry formulation. From the perspective of changing the distribution of slurry abrasive on the surface of polishing pad, the following two factors were mainly studied, namely slurry abrasive size and the amount of surface modifier of slurry abrasive. The results indicated that when abrasive size was ∼50nm and the amount of surface modifier was 1.2% (normalized), the thickness profile response show better linearity to pressure tuning, and the stability of the wafer edge thickness profile in the continuous process is greatly improved, with an increase of more than 95%.

articleTitle: Optimization of 8T SRAM BIT-Cell Design
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, the simulation result reveals that write failure exists on the original two-port bitcell and with the optimized design, the write ability is improved by >66% over the normal 6T SRAM bitcell. A composite failure mode for 8T SRAM write operation was proposed according to the simulation data. Besides, the advantage of two-port SRAM, that the separated read port has no impact on write margin (WRM), has been clarified by decoupled circuit simulation for the first time. Simulations are performed using cadence virtuoso tool.

articleTitle: A Novel RRAM-Based TCAM Search Array
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This work proposes a novel resistive random-access memory (RRAM)-based ternary content-addressable memory (TCAM) array architecture utilizing a Pt/Ta2O5/ZnO/Cu memristive device structure. A compact behavioral model for the memristor is developed based on experimental I-V characterization. A 2T2R cell design is presented leveraging the RRAM device as the storage element co-integrated with CMOS access transistors. An entire TCAM array is designed by arranging the 2T2R cells in a matrix structure. The content search operation is validated through circuit-level simulations using a commercial tool (Virtuoso). Compared to conventional CMOS-only implementations, this proposal offers advantages such as reduced layout area and static power consumption due to the non-volatility of resistive switching memory and is compatible with front-end CMOS processes. This work demonstrates the feasibility of utilizing RRAM devices to implement low-power TCAMs, paving the way for future energy-efficient in-memory search applications.

articleTitle: Effects of Polyvinyl Alcohol on Silicon Chemical Mechanical Polishing
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The effect of polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) in alkaline slurry on the silicon wafer surface during chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) was investigated. This investigation found that PVA is adsorbed onto the colloidal silica abrasive and silicon wafer surface, and that the adsorption amount increases in accordance with PVA concentration. Characterization and analysis were given by measuring the pH, viscosity, removal rate, the adsorption amount of PVA on the surface of colloidal silica particles, contact angle and local point defects of silicon wafer surface.

articleTitle: Preemptive FPGA Scheduling Based on Dynamic Partial Reconfiguration
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: With the increasing scaling of computation workloads, heterogenous computing systems including different kinds of computing platforms such CPU, GPU or FPGA become increasingly important. To exploit the parallelism of FPGA within a heterogenous system, dynamic partial reconfiguration is a powerful technique to enable the FPGA dynamically changes its workload in execution, and hence implement a scheduler which can schedule more tasks to meet their deadlines.

articleTitle: Effect of Green Additive Sarcosine as Inhibitor for Cobalt-Based Copper Interconnect CMP
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) is one of the most effective methods to achieve atomic-scale smooth surface. Each component of the slurry plays an important role in the CMP process. The effect of sarcosine as inhibitors for cobalt-based Cu interconnected CMP was studied in this article. And its mechanism of action was analyzed by electrochemical experiments and atom force microscope (AFM).

articleTitle: Correlation Between CD/LWR and Focus Level Fitting Error: A Process Quality Indicator
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Achieving uniformity of patterns on photoresists is a significant challenge as process nodes get smaller. In practical production lines, the level sensor (LS) of the lithography system will record the focus level to calculate fitting errors and correct the focus level errors automatically during exposure. In this study, we present the analysis of the inherent adjustment errors stemming from the LS process dependency. Additionally, we propose a correlation analysis method that utilizes the focus level fitting errors alongside the measured data including uniformity of critical dimension (CD) and line width roughness (LWR). The correlation can serve as an indicator of process quality and offer guidance for further process optimization.

articleTitle: Model of Organic Ferroelectric Transistors for Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: FeFETs are promising for memory computing in neural networks. Organic ferroelectric materials offer benefits like affordability, scalability, flexibility, and low-temperature processing over their inorganic counterparts. This work introduces a sophisticated physics-based OFeFET model that captures the relationship between capacitive layer thickness and coercive electric field in organic ferroelectric capacitors. The model, validated against a 300 nm P(VDF-TrFE) OFeFET, was integrated into Neurosim to evaluate image recognition performance. Achieving up to 94% accuracy, this work bolsters the potential of organic memory devices in computational applications.

articleTitle: Study on the Slurry for Chemical Mechanical Polishing of GaN Wafer
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The effects of oxidants in acidic and alkaline slurries on the chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) process of gallium nitride were studied. In order to better understand the enhancement effect of oxidants on GaN CMP performance, a reference experiment was established in this study. The experimental results show that SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-based slurry has good performance under acidic conditions, especially in terms of material removal rate (MRR). In addition, K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf> has a higher MRR and lower surface roughness (Sq) than H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> under acidic conditions. The use of SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-based slurry containing K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf> can effectively produce a smooth GaN surface in addition to the classical CMP process.

articleTitle: Exploring Low-Frequency Noise Behavior in Vertically Structured Organic Schottky Photodiodes
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This study delves into low-frequency noise behavior in organic photodiodes (OPD) using DPPT-TT, a prominent organic polymer. Utilizing the 9812D lowfrequency noise test platform, we systematically examined noise patterns at varying voltage levels. The investigation integrates the Hooge low-frequency noise analysis model to elucidate the nature of noise types, carrier transport mechanisms, and generation-recombination (g-r) noise phenomena, especially under high-voltage conditions. Key findings reveal a transition in noise behavior: at bias voltages below 0.9V, the noise predominantly resembles 1/f noise. However, a distinct shift to g-r noise characteristics is observed above this threshold, attributed to increased band bending and the consequent proximity of defect energy levels to the Fermi level under high bias voltages. These insights offer a crucial theoretical framework for understanding the noise characteristics in DPPT-TT organic semiconductors and pave the way for exploring the transport mechanisms in various devices based on this material.

articleTitle: Effect of Green Corrosion Inhibitors on the Performance of Copper-Cobalt CMP
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In cobalt-based copper interconnected copper film chemical mechanical polishing (CMP), corrosion inhibitors have an important influence on the surface quality after polishing. The effects of hypoxanthine and sarcosine as corrosion inhibitors on the performance of copper-cobalt CMP were investigated. The results showed that a strong step height correction capability and a high selectivity ratio of copper and cobalt removal rate were obtained and practiced the concept of green environmental protection.

articleTitle: A Physical Based 2D Monte Carlo Simulation of MO-ECRAM Programming for Device Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Three-terminal metal-oxide electrochemical random-access memory (MO-ECRAM) with high switching linearity has attracted much attention in the novel neuromorphic computing field. In this work, a 2D atomistic Monte Carlo simulation is developed based on the dynamic behaviors of oxygen vacancies. The simulation can quantify the linear/nonlinear switching characteristics under various voltage and temperature stresses, which will be beneficial to optimize the performances of MO-ECRAM.

articleTitle: Study on Failure Mechanism of C4 Bump Solder Excursion in CoWoS Package
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: As Moore's Law reaches its limit, the trend of chip development towards advanced packaging is becoming increasingly evident, with Chip on Wafer on Substrate (CoWoS) packaging (2.5D) technology rapidly being adopted by major IC manufacturers due to its advantages. However, the structure of CoWoS package is more complex than other package, its failure analysis (FA) also facing many challenges. This paper analysis the solder excursion of C4 bump and study its failure mechanism in CoWoS package. The flux residue comes from the substrate causes delamination between the solder mask (SM) and under-fill, resulting in solder excursion.

articleTitle: Impact of Thickness Dependent Ferroelectric and Interface Charge Variation on Device-to-Device Variation in Ferroelectric FET
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this work, the film thickness-dependent threshold voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(V_{\text{TH}})$</tex> variation is investigated theoretically through statistical Monte Carlo simulation. An improved VTH variation is found in the 6 nm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Hf}_{0.5}\text{Zr}_{0.5}\mathrm{O}_{2}$</tex> (HZO) gate insulator under the coupling effect of ferroelectric parameters and interface charge density fluctuations, in comparison to thicker HZO films. The increase in trap density significantly deteriorates the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\text{TH}}$</tex> variation, which can be mitigated by the enlarged charge response in the thin film. This work provides a guideline for variation performance improvement in building reliable ultra-scale integrated circuits.

articleTitle: Sige Epitaxy Improved by SI Cap Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: With the chip manufacturing process continues to advance, traditional MOSFET devices are gradually reaching their physical limits. FDSOI technology was considered as an alternative to traditional devices. In the process research of FDSOI PMOS device, it was found that when the gate oxide (GOX) was grown directly on the SiGe channel, the CV curve of the device would hump significantly. According to theoretical analysis, it may be due to the interface state factors that exist because the gate oxide grows directly in the channel. Therefore, a process method of growing a layer of Si cap on SiGe channel and then growing GOX is proposed in this paper. After the growth of GOX, a thin layer of Si Cap is retained to improve the Dit and CV curves of SiGe. The experimental results show that hump of CV curve was improved after adjustment.

articleTitle: The Defect Formation and Reduction of 55NM Ultra-Low Power (55ULP) BEOL Process
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, dark field inspection tool is implemented in the detection of three main type defects in 55nm Ultra-low Power (55ULP) back-end-of-line (BEOL) manufacturing: the tiny particle of top metal final deposition, seal ring bulge defect after UTM process, and wafer edge cluster tiny particle after TEON process deposition. More defect can be scanning in new detection condition, and defect mechanisms are deduced with scanning results. Experiments designed for CVD (chemical vapor deposition) optimization scheme demonstrates that thicker Film, prolonger purge time lead to a good residue defect performance, meanwhile both getting rid of gas H2 of top metal via etch amount work for seal ring bulge defect reduction, moreover, offshoring cone to a certain distance contributes to lower wafer edge cluster tiny particle count. Make a summary for future development of 55nm ultra-low power and look forward to the future.

articleTitle: High Performance Wafer Defect Classification Model Based on Feature Fusion and RGB SEM Images
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The intelligent analysis of wafer defects is crucial for enhancing yield management and improving production efficiency. This study proposes an automatic defect classification (ADC) method for RGB SEM images and integrates the features of VGG32 and UNet models through cross-fusion techniques. Experimental results demonstrate significant advantages of RGB SEM images over gray SEM images in defect classification, and the feature cross-fusion model achieves better accuracy compared to individual models.

articleTitle: CEO2 Slurry Post Rinse Condition Research in STI CMP Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Chemical Mechanical Planarization(CMP) is a kind of removal technology, which combines chemical reaction and mechanical grinding to remove the film deposition and make the surface smooth. Shallow trench isolation(STI) layer is an important process in the CMP process which can affect the step height between STI and AA. Cerium dioxide(CEO2) slurry is widely used in the STI-CMP process for its high oxide to nitride selectivity. Different polish step settings lead to different thickness result. The post-rinse process is as important as main polish step for the cerium dioxide slurry. In this research, different post rinse condition of pressure and polish time is studied to reduce the OCD area variation. OCD pad trend up by ladder from pad rinse polish time trend up. Along with wafer rinse pressure and polish time increase, the OCD pad trend down obviously when the oxide and nitride pad keep stable. The results indicated that suitable STI-CMP post pad rinse and wafer rinse setting can be fixed.

articleTitle: The Modeling and Optimization of Line Width Roughness in Polysilicon Gate for Improving the Performance of CMOS Device
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The impact of line width roughness (LWR) on transistor performance is one of the hot research topics in the semiconductor industry. This paper investigates the effect of the LWR on the electrical characteristics of 55nm bulk MOSFETs using power spectral density (PSD). A method is provided for analyzing long range LWR using experimental data. It can effectively predict the impact of LWR on the performance of transistors with different gate lengths under the same process flow. By using different plasma etching mask materials, the roughness of the gate width was successfully reduced by over 1nm, and the transistor leakage was reduced by 60%.

articleTitle: Optimization of Polysilicon Gate Etching Process in SONOS Memory Fabrication
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The etching process of the SONOS structure plays an important role on the storage performance of the memory cell. Lateral etching problem and sidewall angle control are possible problems in the etching process. Lateral etching has a great impact on the gate CD and uniformity. In this study, the bucket-shaped sidewall morphology of the gate resulting from lateral etching was addressed by adjusting the gas composition during the soft-landing step, primarily by removing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Cl}_{2}$</tex>. Additionally, controlling the gate sidewall vertically was achieved by etching polysilicon and the block oxide above it in separate steps.

articleTitle: A 110NM BCD-ON-SOI Technology Offering Best-In-Class Nonvolatile Memory IP for Automotive Application
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: X-FAB's advance 110nm BCD-on-SOI platform technology(XT011) [1] presents two qualified nonvolatile memory intellectual property (NVM IP) macros meeting stringent automotive AEC-Q100 Grade-0 standards. The first IP, XFE, integrates SONOS charge trapping memory for eFlash and EEPROM in a compact macro, boasting a 35.6% size reduction(0.500mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) compared to its 180nm counterpart(XT018) [2] with equal memory density. The second IP utilizes floating-gate polysilicon storage for a One Time Programmable (OTPF) memory macro. Operating on XT011's low-power 1.5V/5.0V CMOS with Copper BEOL, both IPs demonstrate compliance with automotive and high-temperature environment requirements (-40°C to 175°C), ideal for code and data storage (XFE) and as an optimal trimming solution (OTPF), under harsh operating conditions.

articleTitle: TimingDTH: Timing-Driven Placement with Deep Three-Head Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Recently, reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms have shown remarkable performance in chip placement scenarios. In this paper, we present TimingDTH, the first timing-driven RL method with deep three-head network. TimingDTH effectively utilizes the timing features, learns from scratch without pretraining, and generates timing-optimized chip placement results. A novel timing feature extraction method is employed to achieve timing optimization. Experiment is conducted on the ICCAD-2015 benchmark. Compared with the state-of-the-art timing-driven solver DREAMPlace4.0, our approach improves total negative slack (TNS) by 11.54% and worst negative slack (WNS) by 1.72%, while significantly saving runtime by 42.39%.

articleTitle: A Customized Model for Defensing Against Adversarial Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Deep neural networks have been successfully used in various fields but are still vulnerable to adversarial attacks. The bit-plane-based adversarial sample defense model is highly effective but exhibits high demands for resources, making it challenging to deploy on hardware devices with limited resources. This work proposes an implementation of an adversarial sample defense model based on bit-plane under resource constraints and verifies the quantization strategies applicable to optimize the existing bit-plane defense model. Compared with existing bit-plane defense algorithms [6], our approach can effectively reduce resource consumption while maintaining prediction accuracy in resource-constrained scenarios.

articleTitle: Improving Gate Oxide Uniformity Using Wet-Dry Oxidation for Semiconductor Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The uniformity of gate oxide is essential to the semiconductor manufacturing process. An unsatisfactory uniformity can lead to a decrease in device performance and yield. This work studies the uniformity of gate oxide film formed in three ways, including dry oxidation, wet oxidation and a sequential process of wet oxidation followed by dry oxidation (wet-dry). The uniformity of gate oxide film decreases as temperature rises between 750 ~ 900°C, and as the gas flow increases. The wet-dry process can maintain a high uniformity at relatively high thickness compared to wet and dry processes. This work will be beneficial to achieving the ideal process window for the target gate oxide film.

articleTitle: α-In2Se3/MoTe2 Heterojunction for P-Type Junction Field-Effect Transistors with Ferroelectric Memory Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors are promising channel materials in field-effect transistors (FETs) to face the challenges at the ultimate scaling limit. N-channel FETs based on 2D materials have been widely explored and exhibit superior performance at the atomic thickness. However, the performance of p-type FETs remains inadequate. Furthermore, the demand for functional integration in electronic devices draws great attention to the study of ferroelectric 2D semiconductors, owing to their combined ferroelectric and semiconductor properties. In this paper, we present a p-channel junction field-effect transistor (PJFET) utilizing MoTe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> as the p-type channel and α-In<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> as the n-type ferroelectric gate, forming a van der Waals PN heterojunction. This strategy enables PJFET with storage functionality and steep subthreshold swing, opening new avenues for innovative transistor-memory architecture.

articleTitle: High Aspect Ratio Carbon Hard Mask Etch Process for Profile and LCDU Control
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Improving the bowing profile and LCDU in HAR etching is challenging due to ion sputtering, insufficient sidewall protection, and uneven polymer deposition. To address these challenges, we investigated the gas ratio in deep hole etching of ACL, the effect of new polymer gas on sidewall protection, and the effects of different descum steps and their addition times and BRF parameters on LCDU. From the results, it can be seen that using more COS in the early stage of etching and adding polymer gas SiCl4 all have varying degrees of improvement on bowing profile. Using a descum step containing CHF3, adding it earlier and using lower BRF resulted in different levels of improvement in LCDU.

articleTitle: Colloidal Quantum Dot Enhanced Short-Wavelength Infrared Absorption of Avalanche Photodetectors
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Avalanche Photodetectors (APDs) are characterized by high gain, fast response, and high sensitivity while operating under a certain bias voltage. Unfortunately, due to the limitations of the silicon material, silicon-based APDs are not sensitive enough to detect wavelengths beyond 1100 nm, which restricts their applications in various fields. One possible solution to detect short-wave infrared (SWIR) light is coating colloidal quantum dots (CQDs) with a tunable energy bandgap on the silicon surface of APD. In this study, an APD using colloidal lead sulfide (PbS) quantum dot material with engineered energy bands is designed, enhancing the short-wavelength infrared sensing capabilities. Through TCAD simulation, the detector is demonstrated to have a responsivity of 8.1 A/W, a quantum efficiency (QE) of 647%, a rise time of 0.52 ns, and a fall time of 3 ns at 1550 nm. The optimized device structure and doping configuration are of benefit to a high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Furthermore, the compatibility of this approach with CMOS technology and the low-cost colloidal quantum dots synthesis significantly reduces the costs of real-time applications in short-wavelength infrared range.

articleTitle: Fea of Thermo-Mechanically Induced Cracks in IMD
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Thermo-mechanical stability in back-end-of-line (BEOL) interconnect structures remains as one of the BEOL integration challenges as coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) mismatch between interconnect metal and dielectric materials resulted in significant thermal stress that often leads to cracks in BEOL structures. These cracks further pose reliability concerns as the cracks may continue to propagate under subsequent thermal loading. Hence, this paper discusses the use of finite element analysis (FEA) along with limited experimental investigation to study the thermo-mechanical stress during BEOL fabrication process and a more conservative approach in evaluating the various process/design factors to reduce the occurrence of inter-metal dielectric (IMD) cracks.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Reusable Structure of I/O Pads for Scan Chains
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: With the increasing complexity of integrated circuits, there is a serious mismatch between the number of I/O pads and scan chains. To solve the above problem, this paper presents a reusable structure of I/O pads for scan chains, which can reallocate I/O resources dynamically and achieve an optimal state after chip manufacturing. The I/O pads and the input/output of the scan chains are connected through the scan I/O reuse logic, which is controlled by the configure chains in the tap controller. Therefore, the scan I/O reuse logic can be dynamically gated by configuring the tap controller.

articleTitle: Performance-Enhanced CMOS Polysilicon Microbolometer with Narrow Supporting Arms
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The performance of a microbolometer can be significantly impacted by the structure of its supporting arms. In this study, we successfully enhanced the performance of a CMOS microbolometer by reducing the width of its supporting arms through a post-CMOS process. The microbolometer with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3\ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> L-type supporting arms demonstrates an ultra-low thermal conductance of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.26\times 10^{-7}\mathrm{W}/\mathrm{K}$</tex> and a maximum responsivity (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{\mathrm{v}}$</tex>) of about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.96\times 10^{4}\mathrm{V}/\mathrm{W}$</tex> at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$25\ \mu \mathrm{A}$</tex>. The average responsivity of the microbolometer is improved by 66.2% from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$7 \mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$13\ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> compared to the microbolometer with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5\ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> supporting arms. The demonstrated high-performance CMOS microbolometer with narrow supporting arms holds a simple structure and preparation process, which is promising for high-density array integration.

articleTitle: Advanced Digital Baseband Signal Generation and Processing Solution for V93000 5G Small Cell Transceiver Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Since the commercialization of 5G, 5G macro base stations have achieved large-scale outdoor signal coverage. Correspondingly, the demand for indoor coverage is also growing continuously. 5G Small Cell, as a means of indoor and deep coverage, possess characteristics such as low power consumption, low cost, and easy deployment. The RF transceiver is a crucial component in the 5G Small Cell. It integrates A/D and D/A modules to enable the conversion between digital baseband signals and RF signals. Hence, we must achieve cross-domain digital and RF signal measurements in ATE testing. We have developed an advanced generation and process solution for digital baseband signals with CMOS and LVDS digital interfaces, which can also be applied to similar RF device testing. This paper will use AD9361 as an example to mainly introduce the digital baseband signal generation and processing solution, Chinese 5G Small Cell market trends, and an overview of mainstream RF testing items.

articleTitle: SMT Optimization of PMOSFET Based on Multi-Deposition and In-Situ N2 Plasma Treatment
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The implementation of stress memory technique (SMT) can indeed improve the performance of NMOSFET. However, it results in the degradation of PMOSFET which is attributed to the hydrogen diffusion and loss of boron in the PMOS. Therefore, we gave a new SMT process, in which strained SiN film deposition was performed by several rounds together with in-situ N2 plasma treatment during former rounds, thereby reducing the amount of hydrogen diffused and the loss of boron, to enhance the PMOS performance.

articleTitle: Reliability Challenges in SIC Components – Performing Dynamic Test Methodologies Like DGS for Meaningful Measurement Results
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Switching a SiC MOSFET using a bipolar gate-source voltage causes drift of the gate-source threshold voltage and the on-resistance. This paper describes the setup used for dynamic gate stress tests of discrete SiC MOSFETs as well as the results. It compares the drift across applied gate-source voltages, frequencies, temperatures, and manufacturers.

articleTitle: Effect of Low Damage Strip Process on Sige Surface State
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Effect of low damage strip process on SiGe surface state under ICP and MARS mode is studied in this paper. FG-based current density in MARS mode is around 10 times lower than that of ICP mode. Ge rich interface is found between Si-O and SiGe layers after treatment process. Valence state can be tailored by various gas composition and plasma activation mode in strip process. Oxidation thickness and valence state are different for the surface of SiGe sample with various treatment conditions, including ICP and MARS mode.

articleTitle: Streamlining Chip Testing with Simplified Digital Data Acquisition
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Digital data acquisition is an indispensable element of chip testing, constituting a fundamental prerequisite for analyzing chip performance within a spectrum of testing modules. The advent of a versatile digital data acquisition tool can dramatically amplify the user-friendliness and operational efficiency of ATE test programs. During ATE testing, engineers frequently engage in manual configuration of capture points to accumulate data at specific vector time points. With the implementation of SMT8, we have efficiently streamlined this procedure through simplified code configurations. Nonetheless, the ever-evolving testing conditions necessitate recurrent code updates. To elevate user experience and streamline ATE operations, we have introduced a standardized library. This library empowers users to flexibly configure parameter sources, showcasing diverse parameter input interfaces. This library empowers developers to expeditiously construct digital capture tests. It caters to both neophytes and seasoned professionals, offering a malleable data input structure, simplifying verification, and furnishing an array of execution and result retrieval interfaces suited to multifarious purposes.

articleTitle: Full Wafer Combinatorial Deposition With In-Situ XPS/UPS Characterizations
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: An 8-inch full wafer cluster tool has been developed, consisting of a combinatorial PVD chamber, a combinatorial ALD chamber and a XPS/UPS chamber. The deposition chambers can achieve up to 8 separate deposition sites on one wafer. Within each site, films can be deposited with either reactive co-sputtering up to 4 targets, or with ALD from up to 3 precursors. The deposition is performed one site at a time with independent process parameters. The uniformity is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< 3.5{\%}$</tex> wi thin site and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< 2{\%}$</tex> for site to site. The wafer can be transferred to the XPS/UPS chamber without breaking vacuum, allowing in-situ characterization of film surface compositions, valence states and work-functions. We believe this is the first report of 8-inch full wafer in-situ XPS capability.

articleTitle: Flexible Low-voltage, Hysteresis-free Ferroelectric Polymer Transistors
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The flexibility and low power consumption are of great significance for the research of polymer transistors, especially in the field of Internet of Things (IoT) and wearable electronics. To achieve low power consumption, it is necessary for the device to operate at low operating voltages while having a small subthreshold swing (SS). Here, by combining ferroelectric Hf<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>Zr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (HZO) gating, high mobility polymer semiconductor film and van der Waals (vdW) integrated process, we realize flexible polymer field-effect transistors (PFET) that deliver low SS (around 100 mV/dec) and two-volt operating voltage. Ferroelectric gate booster enables better switching characteristics of the device, while the vdW process ensures atomically flat metal/semiconductor contacts, which is crucial for device performance. This work provides an additional direction for the further development of flexible, low-power PFETs.

articleTitle: Precise Etching Technique of Ultra-Thin Al2O3 Film Using BCl3 Chemistry
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Precise technique can remove Al2O3 film slowly and evenly by adjusting the gas ratio, pressure, power, temperature and other parameters in ICP plasma. The volatile will release occurs during a physical bombard between a gaseous reactant and the surface modified layer. In this study, BCl3 and Ar/He plasma were used to carry out precise surface etching of Al2O3 layer. Overall this technique has the potential at low temperature for ~50A Al2O3 etching process in semiconductor integration.

articleTitle: The Effect of Depth, AIR Gap Width and ION Implant on Deep Trench Isolation for BCD Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The voltage capability requested to power devices typically spans from 5 V up to 100 V mainly for automotive applications. Owning to the better isolation performance and device integration, deep trench isolation (DTI) is widely used in medium and high voltage grade BCD devices as the substitute for junction isolation. In this study, a combination of simulation and experimental research was employed in systematic investigation of trench depth, air gap width and implant to the device performance. We found that the depth of DTI needs to be at least 24 um for BCD devices with voltage capabilities greater than 100V. The existence of air gap inside DTI and ion implant at DTI bottom can also substantially improve the breaking voltage and prevent leakage. This work presents an optimized DTI structure which can addressed to high voltage (over 100 V) BCD technology platform.

articleTitle: The Influence of Etching Sequence on Morphology in Deep Silicon Etching
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The cycli etching process is mainly used for silicon etching, which can achieve a large aepect ratio and selectivity ratio. The article uses CL2/Ar ase the main etching gas, O2 as the passivation gas, and CF4/CHF3 as the gas for opening the bottom of passivation layer. The result show that the silicon sidewall angle ≥ 96°, the silicon sidewall is continuous, and there is no obvious fan-shaped roughness.

articleTitle: Improvement of Nldmos Performance in Low-Resistivity Substrate for Integration with Discrete Power Devices on One Chip
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Discrete power device is usually manufactured separately from logic devices due to the limitation of utilizing low-resistivity substrates. This paper presents an NLDMOS capable of being manufactured together with discrete devices on one chip based on TCAD simulation. The NLDMOS is designed in heavily doped N-type epi and isolated by a wide PBL which is picked up using a deep P-well in body region. The performance of the NLDMOS is enhanced by optimizing the ion implantation at its drain region: N+ is shifted 0.3um away from the edge of STI to increase the on-state breakdown voltage; a RESULF boron region is deeply implanted at the bottom of N-drift region to increase the off-state breakdown voltage. Therefore, a high on-BV and off-BV NLDMOS is achieved in a low-resistivity substrate, which could be further integrated with discrete devices on one chip.

articleTitle: TSV Integrated and Pattern Recognition Based Multimode Degenerated Low-Power 3-Dimensional Smart Sensing Chips
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This paper demonstrates a low-power designed and highly integrated multimode sensor chip that employs wafer level packaging and TSV based 3D integration to ensure high integrated density, high flexibility and high reliability. Through-silicon vias (TSVs) can be adopted to extract electrodes from the back or cross of the wafer to achieve shared integrated circuits, miniaturization of devices and anti-interference capabilities. The integrated multimode sensing chips based on 3D packaging realize the miniaturization of high-performance chips and further provide opportunities for pattern recognition based multimode single-device sensing chips. This unique technology solutions can achieve high compatibility and high packaged manufacturing according to different needs and can be widely applied to various microsystem chips.

articleTitle: A Photoeletric Memristive Device for Artificial Visual Perception
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Optoelectronic neuromorphic devices have driven the effective development of artificial vision systems, thanks to their ability to capture, store, and process visual information in the environment. We propose a single transistor based optoelectronic memristor that modulates the resistance of MOS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> channels through photo-generated carriers, affects the voltage bias of the threshold switch (TS) drain, and achieves the basic neural functions of simulating leakage integration and excitation (LIF) and depolarization. Single transistor neurons drive the efficient development of neuromorphic systems.

articleTitle: Study of Tungsten-Doped Carbon Hard Mask Etch Process Using NF3/O2 Based Chemistry
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Tungsten-doped carbon (WDC) materials have been investigated as a hard mask material because of high etching resistance in via and contact holes manufacture integration. This article studied the etching process of WDC in O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> based plasma with an added reactant source such as Cl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> or NF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> chemistry. A series of orthogonal design of experiment (DOE) was utilized to analyze the etch rate data. The results showed that the NF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> addition can significantly enhance WDC etch rate, compared to Cl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> addition. The etch selectivity of WDC to silicon oxide (SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) mask is increased as using synchronic pulsed RF powers, adding BCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and reducing ESC temperature.

articleTitle: Logic Synthesis for XOR-AND Graphs via Reed-Muller Representations
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Logic synthesis, as a key step in the design flow of modern integrated circuits, plays an important role in the development of emerging technologies and quantum computing. XOR-AND graphs (XAGs) is used to express Boolean functions that are widely used in cryptographic security application. In this paper, we propose a new rewriting approach based on the Reed-Muller (RM) logic expansion. To find an area-efficient representation of the logic network, the cuts of the logic network are enumerated and then the RM logic expansion based on mixed polarities is utilized. By conducting the experiments over EPFL benchmarks, we achieve a maximum reduction of 50% in the number of XOR gates and a normalized geometric mean of 25%.

articleTitle: Inflection Points in Cfet Scaling: Impact of Dtco Boosters
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Complimentary FETs (CFETs) enable aggressive standard cell height (CH) reduction, facilitating on-target area scaling without shrinking contacted gate pitch (CGP). We extensively benchmark nanosheet (NS) based CFETs against gate-all-around (GAA) NSFETs using power, performance, area (PPA) as well as scalability metrics. The impact of BEoL RC, new materials, DTCO boosters is further explored. 4T CFET designed with 20 nm metal pitch (MP) offers 62% smaller area and 28% extra speed at iso-power over reference NS devices.

articleTitle: EOE Evolution Processes of Same Step Profile With Different One-Material Polishing Time in CMP
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Edge over Erosion (EOE) is frequently observed in chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) process. It is found in the simulation results that the initial profile of two-material polishing stage has a great effect on the evolution of EOE. In this paper, five initial profiles of F1~F5 are obtained by using different one-material polishing time with same step profile. The evolution processes of the initial profiles of F1~F5 with selectivity ratio <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> are simulated and the EOE are given. The relationship between the initial profiles and the EOE evolution processes is investigated.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) Based Process Window Analysising for Lithography
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Efficient and highly accurate methods and tools for process window analysis are urgently needed in integrated circuit manufacturing. We have developed a convolutional neural network-based automated process window analysis tool, which can analyze process windows from raw data efficiently. Our tool utilizes convolutional neural network and well-trained models for classifying critical dimension scanning electron microscope images to enhance efficiency and reduce errors for process window analysis. Furthermore, we propose an image segmentation-based classification method to further improve accuracy. The proposed method is potential for expedited and highly accurate process window analysis.

articleTitle: Design of a 10-BIT 100MSPS Sar ADC
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This paper reports a 10-bit 100-MS/s SAR ADC using a novel bootstrap switching circuit. The Vcm-based switching time sequence is used to ensure that the comparator has a stable and constant common-mode input voltage during operation. By using split capacitors to avoid the introduction of VDD/2 voltage sources, a segmented DAC array is designed to effectively reduce the capacitance of CDAC. A two-stages dynamic comparator was used to reduce power consumption and noise. At 100M sampling rate and 1.2v supply voltage, the ADC consumes 4.25m W and achieves an SNDR of 60.69dB, resulting in an FOM of 48fJ/Conversion-step. Fabricated in a 40nm 1P6M CMOS technology, the ADC only occupies 0.075mm2 active area.

articleTitle: A First-Principles Study on the Stable Phase in Yttrium-Doped HFO2
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Hafnium oxide has been widely used in IC processes, but the explanation of its stable ferroelectricity remains controversial. This article investigated the effects of yttrium doping on the properties of HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> through first-principles calculations. The results illustrated that the formation energy of oxygen vacancy is 17.8% lower with yttrium doping. In highly oxygen-deficient YHf<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>o<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>, the cubic phase is stable and the monoclinic-cubic phase transition barrier is reduced by 39%. The doping-defect coupling model is expected to explain the ferroelectric behavior in Y -doped HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>.

articleTitle: New Methodology for Anisotropic Nanoparticles Characterization by Depolarized Light Scattering Measurements: Length and Diameter Determination of Rod-Like Nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this work, we introduce a new setup and a method for characterizing anisotropic nanoparticles using a multi-angle polarization dynamic light scattering technique. This method is based on the measurement of the correlograms of scattered light intensity fluctuations both in the parallel and crossed polarizer configurations, and possibly concomitantly, from which the rotational and translational diffusion coefficients are extracted. By inversing the mathematical expressions of these coefficients, this approach allows the rapid determination of length and diameter of the anisotropic nanoparticles, enabling kinetic measurements. A comparison of experimental results obtained with this multi-angle depolarized DLS (DDLS) method to classical TEM images is discussed.

articleTitle: Application of Community Detection Based Parallel MOEA/D Algorithm in RF Power Amplifier Circuit Design
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Radio frequency (RF) power amplifier (PA) plays a crucial role in modern communication systems, and designing RF PA that meets various performance specifications (Specs) has become increasingly difficult due to the complex design space [1]. This work proposes a community detection based parallel MOEA/D algorithm (CD-PMOEA/D) for RF PA design automation. The proposed approach shortens the design cycle by at least 3X and achieves ∼5% higher performance than that of the traditional MOEA/D method. As demonstrations, a common source PA with three optimization objectives is successfully designed within 1 hour, at a working frequency bandwidth of 23GHz-25GHz and reached a Power Gain of 14.3dB, OP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1dB</inf> of 17.9dBm, and DE@OP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1dB</inf> of 53.8%. A cascode PA with five optimization objectives at a working frequency of 28GHz is also successfully designed with similar time expenses, meeting all performance specifications. This work paves a new way for RF PA circuit design automation.

articleTitle: Static Leakage Failure Analysis and Improvement for Small Size Sram
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Static random access memory (SRAM) is widely used in sensing applications and in a wide variety of other ASIC and system chips. In order to obtain the maximum SRAM capacity while further reducing the chip area, SRAM usually uses the minimum size allowed by the corresponding technology node. However, when the process size is reduced, the static leakage current of the SRAM memory unit will increase, which will lead to an increase in the static power consumption of the system or chip. Therefore, it is of great significance to design a small-size SRAM with low leakage power consumption and satisfactory performance. In this paper, based on the SRAM structure with mature technology and mass production, the size of the SRAM is miniaturized by 20% to develop a smaller size of SRAM, and the static leakage of small size SRAM unit is improved by failure analysis and process optimization. As the distance between the polysilicon gates of small size SRAM unit decreases, the static leakage current becomes larger due to the gate oxygen tunneling current caused by too large contact hole and the PN junction reverse bias current caused by poor growth of metal silicide. By reducing the size of the contact hole and optimizing the growth conditions of the metal silicide, the static leakage current of small size SRAM is reduced to less than 70 μA, fully meeting the design requirements of 150 μA.

articleTitle: A Study on Bevel Metal Film Removal for Bevel Peeling Defect Reduction
