publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: With logic technology reached 28nm and beyond, wafer bevel peeling defect is becoming one of the major yield killers. One of the most important sources is the mismatched stress induced by BEOL bevel metal films. In this work, firstly, the mechanism of wafer bevel peeling defects caused by bevel metal films is studied. Then, backside wet etching process is introduced to remove the bevel metal films to reduce the peeling defect. Thirdly, we successfully solve the undercut issue generated during backside wet etching process via optimize the process conditions. Finally, a good result with better bevel metal film removal with defect count has been reduced by 200% and free of undercut is achieved through optimizing process conditions of backside wet etching process.

articleTitle: The Impact of Wafer Warpage-Induced Unevenness on Alignment
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Accurate alignment of patterns on different layers using alignment marks is a challenge, where poor alignment results in overlay errors or even risks wafer rejection especially when dealing with curved wafers. In this study, we utilized the finite difference time domain (FDTD) simulation to evaluate the impact of surface flatness on the quality of signals of alignment marks. Our simulation established a simplified model to reflect surface non-uniformities. The results reveal that non-uniformities can cause a decrease in diffraction signal intensity. This indicates the critical influence of surface non-uniformities on alignment quality, offering valuable implications for process optimization.

articleTitle: Analog Device Engineering and Enhancement in 0.18μm BCD on SOI Technology Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Analog primitive development and advancing are essential to provide a competitive technology portfolio while complimenting the CMOS digital part, HV, NVM offer for various product application. A variety of analog primitives have been designed and offered in X-FAB XT018 BCD on SOI technology [1] [2] since its production release. These devices are popular and widely used in customer product designs. This paper has summarised the past development and possible future advancing works for different analog primitives of this technology.

articleTitle: Calculation Method of Target Erosion in the Planar DC Magnetron Sputtering
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The method of prediction of targets erosion in Direct Current Magnetron Sputtering System(DC-MSS) is suggested. The calculation model assume that the distribution of plasma is the same as the horizontal magnetic field distribution of magnetron. We use COMSOL Multiphysics to simulate the horizontal magnetic field and divide it into tangential and radial components. The radial magnetic field is independent of velocity, and we calculate the target erosion based on the static state of the magnetron. The tangential magnetic field is related to velocity, and we calculate the target erosion based on the rotation state of the magnetron. Finally, we will sum the radial and tangential magnetic field to obtain the target erosion. The calculated target erosion is in very good agreement with the measured of a real large size target used. This calculation method will be valuable in designing the magnet arrangement of a magnetron in DC-MSS.

articleTitle: Structure Optimization of 4X NM Nor Flash for Improving Cell Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: ETOX devices with high-tech nodes offer superior PGM/ERS efficiency, but there are challenges in maintaining PGM/ERS Vt window when developing more advanced technical node. In this paper, a feasible optimization strategy is proposed to improve attenuation of Vt Windows in shrunken ETOX NOR Flash. Based on the technological parameters of 4X nm NOR Flash, the CG filling window is adjusted by increasing the amount of etching in the nitride pullback to improve the coverage ratio of CG on FG. Therefore, the gate coupling ratio of device is optimized. In addition, it shows the same trend in traditional cell that Vt window can be enhanced by optimizing the coupling ratio. On the one hand, it provides an efficient PGM/ERS strategy for shrunken NOR Flash, on the other hand, the widened FG space increases the CG filling window. The experimental results after process optimization show that the Vt window is improved by at least 10% and obtain an extra 10% for CG filling Window in tiny cell.

articleTitle: Study on the Dispersing Effect and Mechanism of Labsa on SiO2 in an Alkaline Barrier Slurry
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) slurry, the introduction of oxidizers, corrosion inhibitors, and other components often leads to the aggregation of SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. In this paper, the dispersing effect and mechanism of anionic surfactants linear alkyl benzenesulfonic acid (LABSA) on colloidal silica in a weakly alkaline slurry for cobalt barrier layer were investigated by experimental and simulation methods. The results show that the doublelayer adsorption formed by a high concentration of deprotonated LABSA can effectively disperse SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> particles.

articleTitle: Sources of Dark Current in Backscattered Electron Detectors and a Novel Multiple Guard Ring Design to Lower It
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Backscattered electron detector (BSD) is a key component in electron-based microscopies. To achieve a high-performance BSD, in other words, a detector with high signal-to-noise ratio, minimizing the dark current is crucial. In this study, the dark current of BSD was systematically investigated considering the impact of surface damages, contamination, and moisture. To reduce the dark current, a novel multiple guard ring structure is proposed and optimized, taking into account parameters including the width of guard ring and gaps between the active area and guard rings. Compared to the commonlyused single guard ring structure, the simulated results indicate that the proposed multiple guard ring structure effectively decreases the dark current to 0.25 nA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, while the breakdown voltage increases to 930V.

articleTitle: Integer Arithmetic-Based and Activation-Aware GELU Optimization for Vision Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The implementation for non-linear activation functions like GELU in Transformer-based model is an challenging problem, especially in pursuit of energy-efficiency and high accuracy. To address this challenge, this paper presents a hardware-friendly optimization method for GELU deployment, an activation-aware strategy with integer arithmetic-based GELU calculation. This method detects activation magnitudes, approximates small and extremely large activation values with linear functions, while a more exact polynomial approximation function is applied to other values to ensure model accuracy. Implemented and evaluated under 22nm CMOS technology, the proposed design can improve the energy-efficiency by 2.14x and area-efficiency by 1.41×, compared with contemporary designs, while the accuracy loss is less than 1 % in Vit, Deit and Swin models.

articleTitle: Mirroring ATPG Technology for Multi-Core Chips
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Multi-core multiplexing scenarios are common in today's ultra-large-scale network system chips and large computing power chips such as CPUs and GPUs. To screen out chips with manufacturing defects and to improve product quality, the traditional automatic test pattern generation(ATPG) method requires large numbers of input and output(I/O) pins. In this paper, a novel idea called Mirroring ATPG is proposed to reduce the I/O resources and improve the efficiency of ATPG test.

articleTitle: Improved EM Performance by Adjusting Etching Profile of Top Metal for 28HK Metal Gate Process
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: EM (Electro Migration) performance is a key item to evaluate the reliability of the integrated circuit production. Nevertheless, with the scaling down of size and more complicated process, reliability has to face various serious challenges. In this work, we adjusted the top metal etching profile in the 28HKMG process and improved the EM performance effectively.

articleTitle: Research on the Substitution of MIM Capacitors and MOM Capacitors on 12-INCH 90-NM BCD Process
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: At present, the capacitors used in the 12-inch 90nm BCD process are still mainly MIM (metal-insulator-metal) capacitors. Compared with MOM (metal-oxide-metal) capacitors, MIM capacitors exhibit more stable capacitive characteristics. However, MOM capacitors do not require additional fabrication masks during the manufacturing process, are easier to produce, and feature high capacitance density. By comparing the voltage linearity, temperature linearity, mismatch performance and WAT (wafer acceptance test) results of MIM capacitors and MOM capacitors on the 12-inch 90nm BCD process, we preliminarily proved the similarity in performance of the two capacitors, indicating the possibility of partially replacing MIM capacitors with MOM capacitors in the future of semiconductor manufacturing.

articleTitle: Plasma Corrosion Resistant Atomic Layer Deposited Coatings for Semiconductor Manufacturing Process Equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Fluoride plasma resistant ALD coatings were developed for coating of semiconductor manufacturing process equipment parts. ALD thin films consisting of Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and Y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> were deposited, characterized and dry etched. The films were high purity with near stoichiometric composition. Plasma etching using example etch processes showed the films were highly resistant to the etching. Y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> mixing into the Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> film had a nonlinear effect on the etch resistance with a rapid increase with low Y fractions and plateauing as pure yttria was approached. Imaging of the etched films showed uniform etching with no preference on the grain boundaries.

articleTitle: The Secret of the Leakage Current Mechanism in Some Historical Device-Quality High-K Metal-Insulator-Metal Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The leakage current mechanism of high-k metal-insulator- metal (MIM) capacitor has been controversial and seems to be some sort of secret. In this paper, a unified Ohmic-Schottky- Poole-Frenkel (O-SPF) theory will be presented. In addition, the effect of charge trapping can be important. The author tried to demonstrate his theory for 15 nm Ta<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> and 5 nm HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> MIM capacitors.

articleTitle: Effect of Lightly Doped Drain Process on Variability for Static Random-Access Memory
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The effect of the lightly doped drain (LDD) implantation process on the variability of six-transistor (6T) static random-access memory (SRAM) cells at a V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DD</inf> value of 1.2 V was investigated. It is found that the variability of static noise margin in the hold, read, and write states decreased with the increase of LDD implantation dose, indicating that increased LDD dose contributes to improving the variability of SRAM cells.

articleTitle: Anomaly Detection of Cdsem Images
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In semiconductor manufacturing factories, Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) are widely used for critical dimension metrology, process control inspection and defects analysis. There are lots of times to measure the after developing inspection (ADI) and after etching inspection (AEI) in the process. And it's a waste time and energy thing for engineers to distinguish between normal and abnormal images. Here, we used unsupervised anomaly detection to analyze CD-SEM images. We used an autoencoder which has an encoder-decoder-encoder pipeline, and capture the training data distribution within both image and latent vector space. And the result indicated that this method could save engineers' time on distinguishing normal and abnormal CD-SEM images

articleTitle: Influence of FOUP Environment on Defects in Semiconductor Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This Paper mainly studies the influence of Foup Environment On Defects in Semiconductor manufacturing. The influence of the change of the interval environment of the foup on the wafer defects gradually appears with the continuous reduction of the semiconductor size. This paper focuses on introducing the defects related to the internal environment of the foup and the mechanism of the defect generation. Which factors in the mechanism are related to the environment. This Paper introduces two types of defects related to the internal environment of the foup.

Author Keywords: the Conditions of the internal environment of FOUP

articleTitle: Tiny Neural Network Representing Mosfet Physical Effect Sub-Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Tiny neural network (NN) modeling physical effects inside MOSFET is demonstrated in this work. BSIM-IMG and HSPICE are used to generation datasets, which samples above 20000. Physical effects, Threshold Voltage Roll-off (TVR) and DIBL, are set as NN modeling goal and achieved >99% and >92% fitting accuracy respectively (@ 5-100-100-42 FCN, 15 training epochs). The conception of cooperation between multi NN-based sub-model and BSIM core-model is also verified (accuracy >95%).

articleTitle: Various Driver Test Summary on V93000 in Automotive Device
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Due to the technique iteration of automotive chip, the devices are becoming much more complex. Thus, various types of drivers are involved in different system, such as HS/LS driver, high-side/low-side switch, ignition driver, valve driver and so on. These drivers will be applied to pyro fuse systems, engine management system, alternator electronics… In this paper, it will introduce three kinds of driver in automotive device firstly, which have their own different characteristics. Secondly, based on upper real test cases, what is the key and common items in different kinds of driver and strictly automotive quality process based on V93000 platform will be described.

articleTitle: Method of Scalable Polysilicon Resistor by Adjusting Shielding Metal in CMOS Process
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The sheet resistance of polysilicon resistors has been investigated with a split design of metal shielding to the polysilicon resistor body. The design split includes metal level split, shielding metal extension size split to resistor body, and metal shielding ratio to a poly resistor in 0.18um CMOS process. Based on the evaluation results, we found that it's possible to control the sheet resistance of poly resistors by metal-1 shielding design, which allows a scalable polysilicon resistor with different polysilicon sheet resistance with the exact dimensions without any process change or addition. Therefore, the chip designer can control the polysilicon sheet resistance considering the available design area for the resistor. Finally, it will be helpful to minimize the chip size, which will lead to a cost-effective design.

articleTitle: Breakdown Voltage Improvement of LDMOS by CESL Optimization in High-Voltage 90 NM BCD Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The Bipolar-CMOS-DMOS (BCD) technology has been widely used in smart-power application (5–100 V). However, the plasma damage of back end of line (BEOL) restricts its breakdown voltage (BV) of LDMOS in BCD and limits its further application in high voltage field (>100 V). In this paper, we optimize the contact etch stop layer (CESL) to improve the off-B- <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{V}_{\text{ds}}$</tex> of LDMOS in 90 nm BCD technology. Replacing CESL from SiN to SiON can decrease the trapping electrons on the silicon surface and relieve the limitation of off-B <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{V}_{\text{ds}}$</tex> improvement. The optimized NLDMOS exhibits an off-B- <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{V}_{\text{ds}}$</tex> of 130 V, which is 28% higher than the old baseline. These results enable a low cost and simple process for power management applications.

articleTitle: New Insight into Impacts from Read Cycle Number and Voltage Sweeping Direction on Memory Window of Ferroelectric Fet
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this work, impacts from cycle number and direction of sweep voltage on electrical characteristics of ferroelectric FET (FeFET) during readout are investigated. Considering polarization switching dynamics, it is found that the memory window (MW) of FeFET shows large dependence on both sweep time and read cycle number. Under continuous sweep voltage cycles for readout, MW will gradually degrade. Furthermore, MW dependence on sweep direction of gate voltage is demonstrated, showing significant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TH</inf> shift under reverse sweep for erase state. This work provides theoretical analysis for more accurate MW estimation of FeFET.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Performance Prediction Model Optimization for Soi Ldmos Using Adaptive Small Space Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This work proposes an adaptive small space dataset generation approach to improve the ML-based model. By leveraging radial basis function (RBF) kernel to calculate similarity to the target structure, small space training data sets with high similarity are filtered for model training. The numerical results show that the small space model can not only improve the performance prediction accuracy, but also accelerate the model testing process. Meanwhile, the memory requirements during the training process are significantly reduced. In addition, the accuracies of small space models using different algorithms also demonstrate the robustness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An Efficient Library for Protocol Test on V93000
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Modern SoC devices integrate multiple high-level IP cores. The control of these functional blocks usually is programed through interfaces such as JTAG, SPI, I2C, etc. For ATE test, Advantest SmarTest8 platform on V93000 provides Protocol Access library to simplify the register operations. It's a pattern-based software solution programming in Java. The protocol access API provides ways to generate patterns for protocol tests through test method. This paper will introduce an efficient library which is based on protocol access library. It takes the benefits of Protocol Access API and helps engineers to setup the protocol definition easily without touching java code. With this library, the initial study and developing time are greatly speed up. Zero code is needed to define protocols for a new development device. Its implementation is clean and neat.

articleTitle: Reducing Side Cutting During Wet Etching of Gate Oxide Layer for 28HK Metal Gate Process
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In wet etching process, side cutting is a common phenomenon that could cause the gate oxide of high voltage transistor to be thin. In this paper, gate oxide breakdown of high operating transistor is observed for 28nm high-K metal gate process. The failure mechanism is discussed and improvement methods are proposed including layout design optimization and process improvement

articleTitle: A Brief Review on Commonly Used Metal ALD Precursors for Semiconductor from A Structural Chemistry Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This review succinctly examines a few commonly used ALD metalorganic precursors, highlighting their physical and deposition properties. Precursors with similar molecular structures are compared. This concise analysis aims to elucidate the correlations between molecular structure and functional characteristics of ALD precursors, providing insights for their application in thin film deposition.

articleTitle: Sample Preparation Method for In-Situ Tem Analysis in Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In-situ TEM techniques assists process tuning and semiconductor device designing behaviors of materials and devices in response to changing temperature and electrical parameters. However, sample preparation of in-situ TEM is full of challenge. In this work, the selection of deposition material for In-situ TEM sample is demonstrated. Method of In-situ TEM sample preparation with DENS Solution provided 52°/33° stage, is elaborated in terms of its operating procedure, advantages and shortcomings. Finally, 4 in-situ biasing TEM testing configuration, thin film resistance measurement, Cu line electrical migration performance testing, high-resistance material electrical migration performance analysis and gate oxide properties analysis, are briefly discussed respectively.

articleTitle: Line Edge Roughness Reduction in High Aspect Ratio Carbon Hardmask Patterning for Slit Trench
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The amorphous carbon used as the hard mask for the etching of slit trench in flash memory, was etched using O2/COS and pulsed dual-frequency inductively coupled plasma. Line edge roughness(LER) of carbon hard mask will transfer to slit trench and result in severe yield loss. In this paper, lots of methods are proposed to reduce LER. The results show that LER can be significantly improved by reducing deposition, lower bias power and enough time or plasma amounts to remove sidewall polymer.

articleTitle: Address the Challenges of Mass Production Testing for 5G Millimeter Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: At present, China's 5G deployment is mainly in the Sub-6GHz frequency band. With the further improvement of the 5G penetration rate and the rapid expansion of application scenarios, users' demand for 5G has begun to expand towards more segmented fields. In the future, it will gradually shift from low-frequency to high-frequency modes such as low-frequency and millimeter wave. The millimeter frequency band has abundant bandwidth resources, which can greatly improve communication speed and achieve the optimal 5G experience. As the core component of 5G millimeter (5G NR FR2) devices, millimeter chips mostly integrate antennas using advanced packaging technology, which has high requirements for frequency, bandwidth, and OTA test approaches. This paper will introduce 5G millimeter (5G NR FR2) application scenarios, worldwide market trends, device trends, and the testing challenges of such devices, as well as the mass production testing solutions on the ADVANTEST V93000 platform.

articleTitle: Multi-Physics Simulation of Electromigration in Cu Interconnect
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Electromigration (EM) has become a serious reliability concern for Cu interconnects as the feature size of ultra-large-scale interconnects (ULSI) technology is reducing. It is governed by the interaction of various atomic fluxes (AF) due to electron-wind force, temperature and stress gradients, respectively. In this work, the non-uniform distribution of the current density, temperature and stress in Cu interconnects line/via structure was simulated using the finite element method. By coupling the current density, temperature and stress fields in the analysis, and using the site with maximum atomic flux divergence as the void location site, a good correlation between the model predictions and experimental observations is obtained.

articleTitle: IGZO-TA2O5 Dual-Layer Cbrram: A Low Voltage and High Switching Ratio Storage Solution
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This study explores the development and characteristic analysis of a Conductive Bridge Random Access Memory (CBRRAM) device utilizing an IGZO-Ta<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> dual-layer dielectric layer. The device demonstrates significant low threshold voltage, high ON/OFF switching ratio, and stable resistive switching characteristics, especially under a Set voltage less than 0.2V and a Reset voltage below -0.16V. These attributes render it exemplary in the field of non-volatile memory devices, showcasing immense potential and application prospects in high-performance computing and storage applications. The paper details the fabrication process, experimental design, and result analysis of the device [1]–[3], delving into the potential applications and challenges of this CBRRAM device in future storage and computing domains, particularly in areas like the Internet of Things, edge computing, and neuromorphic computing.

articleTitle: Improvement of Warping Simulation Accuracy and Influence Factors Analysis in FCBGA Package
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: With the continuous development of packaging technology, the warping problem has attracted more and more attention, which may lead to reduced solder joint life and TIM coverage, so how to accurately predict package warping becomes particularly important. This paper firstly studies the simulation accuracy of two different methods with 25mm FCBGA package, among which the simulation method based on Birth-and-Death element technology is in good agreement with test results. Then, multi-factor DOEs simulation is carried out to study the influence trend and degree of each factor on warping by changing the factors such as Lid thickness, foot width, Core thickness and core type. It is found that lid thickness and core thickness have significant influence on packaging warpage.

articleTitle: Analysis and Protection Solution for Aging DC-Stress Induced Waveform Distortion Issues
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: As during the idle or clock gated mode, long term DC-stress condition in the timing signal path could result in an obvious waveform change induced by aging degradation, which could bring about timing violation and reliability issue. In this paper, we rely on two cases to reveal and study the impact of long term DC-stress on waveform by means of SPICE simulation. Furtherly, according to the simulation results, some measures are proposed to avoid such waveform change-induced aging timing issues.

articleTitle: A Trade-Off Balance Between CU Corrosion and CU Oxide DEFECT
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Chemical mechanical polishing plays a vital role in back-end Cu interconnection technology, while Cu corrosion and Cu oxide are two killer defects which may cause the poor contact of metal lines. Here, we study the root causes of these two defects and propose our solutions. Results of design of experiment show that the formation of Cu corrosion and Cu oxide are inversely related to the concentration of clean chemical. By a series of attempts from optimizing clean recipe, adding chemical buff step for pre-protection, calibrating the drop point of upper rinse water, changing nozzle type, adjusting chemical concentration etc., we successfully reduce the above two defects in chemical trend down manner.

articleTitle: Spectra Machine Learning for the Prediction of Sheet Resistance and Capacity
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Optical spectra based on ellipsometry and reflectometry provide valuable information about the geometric and dielectric properties of wafers, and thus the correlated electric performance. This work presents a machine learning based method to directly extract the electric information from optical spectra for the prediction of sheet resistance and capacity of metal layers. Both training and testing data shows excellent consistency between predicted results by spectra machine learning and actual results from wafer acceptance test. The optical methodology enables non-destructive and in-situ prediction of electric properties at correlated processes with high inline throughput and sampling rate. Additionally, the model-free machine learning methodology provides the ability to measure the complex structures in wafers with less time to solution and more reserved resources.

articleTitle: Multifunctional RRAM Chip with Configurability for Sparsity-Aware in-Memory ISNG Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The Ising machine is a kind of annealing processor. When a combinatorial optimization problem is mapped on an Ising graph, the Ising machine calculates the physical evolution of this system and solves the problem. RRAM-based in-memory computing (IMC) is an important technique that can build up Ising machines. However, the high sparsity of the Ising graphs still fundamentally limits the time and energy efficiency. In this work, we propose a multifunctional RRAM chip that suits sparsity-aware in-memory computing Ising machine, which contains RRAM accelerated content-addressable memory (CAM), multiply-accumulate (MAC) unit, and true random number generator (TRNG) to work collaboratively. Such RRAM-based Ising machine provides significant improvement in both computing speed and energy consumption.

articleTitle: A New Method for Improving 8V ESD Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In recent years, with the rapid development of High Voltage Driver IC performance, the demand for ESD (Electro-Static Discharge) protection devices has increased. Gate-Grounded NMOS devices (GGNMOS, Gate-grounded NMOS) are commonly used as ESD protection devices. In this paper, IO 8V device is used as the protected device, aiming to improve the performance of GGNMOS by optimizing the process and structure. Experiments show that Holding Voltage and It2 increase with the increase of Channel length, and the increase of Holding Voltage is related to the length of the base area of npn. The increase of the base area will lead to the change of parasitic triode gain and further affect the Holding Voltage;

articleTitle: Study on Ceria Slurry for Chemical Mechanical Polishing of 4H-SiC
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Chemical mechanical polishing technology is an important means for achieving global flatness in integrated circuit manufacturing, and the abrasive, oxidant and additive in the polishing slurry are vital factors that affect the polishing results. This paper investigates the effect of incorporating cationic surfactant based on ceria (CeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) and potassium permanganate (KMnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>) for the material removal rate and the surface quality of silicon carbide (SiC). The polishing slurry is formulated with 2 wt% ceria, 0.025 mol/L KMnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>, and cationic surfactant at pH 4.0. The maximum material removal rate (MRR<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf>) of SiC is 777 nm/h, and the surface roughness (Sq) is 0.06 nm.

articleTitle: A Novel Smart Sampling Approach with Broader Compatibility in Semiconductor Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Inspection is an essential part in semiconductor manufacturing process. Although high inspection rate can ensure early detection of inline abnormality, but still it is strictly controlled due to tight production plan and limitation of inspection tool capacity. Thus, an optimized sampling solution is needed to manage the situation. The proposed solution must be able to comprehensively monitor production equipment status and dynamically adjust the lot sampling plan with high accuracy and ultimate efficiency. To fulfill the requirement, based on smart sampling system proposed in 2010 [1], the work here introduced the concept of sampling threshold to determine the lots to be sampled with better robustness. The simulation result shows that under same sampling rate, the sampling plan controlled by sampling threshold can maintain the production system overall risk at lower level than systematic sampling.

articleTitle: Yield Improvement in 4X Node Technology ETOX NOR Flash by Optimizing Control Gate Related Process and Design
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The cause of 4Xnm NOR-flash low yield and corresponding optimized manufactural process have been investigated in this paper. Some stack poly gate etching recipe splits are done to solve word line bridge formation mechanism. To solve word line bridges problem, we can increase control gate recipe organic bottom anti-reflective coating over etching time. After the process optimization, the control gate poly residues are eliminated and the chip prober yield rate is greatly improved. In addition, a novel design of inserting dummy active area under the control gate ends is proposed to eliminate the word line bridge.

articleTitle: A Study of Flexible BEOL Design Rules Allowing Degreed Slanted Interconenction in Advanced Nodes
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Flexible design rules of BEOL layers have gained widespread attention in advanced integrated circuit technology nodes, with the potential to yield substantial cost savings in manufacturing. In our previous work we have explored a type of 45-degree slanted interconnection in the BEOL layers under 7 nm logic design rules. The lithography aerial image simulation result revealed a promising 10-20% reduction in mask minimum area. In this study, we will extend the investigation to various angled slanted lines in BEOL interconnect layers, focusing on patterns featuring slanted lines with 18.5°–45°. These angles correspond to the connection of two vias at distances of 1–3 metal tracks, respectively. With our self-developed aerial image simulator, the design rules allowing these degreed slanted interconnections will be analyzed. After determining the critical size and minimum area, a comparison with the traditional rectilinear designs will be made to explore the potential advantages of these degreed slanted interconnection in terms of lithography complexity and cost reduction in chip manufacturing.

articleTitle: Substrate Current Improvement and Investigation in Low Voltage Power Ldmos with A Novel Design
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: A lateral double-diffused metal–oxide–semiconductor (LDMOS) field-effect transistor with stepped filed plates (SFP) was investigated in this work. The second substrate current peak was highly suppressed by a novel structure design. The novel SFP-NLDMOS device features an additonal CFP at the dain side. This improvement was verified in our 24V NLDMOS and can be applied to other low-voltage power LDMOS with different FP design if neccessary. It was revealed that the second substrate current peak of 24V NLDMOS was decreased by over 60% within our new design. The electric field at drainside was significantly rudced. Therefore, the kirk effect was hgihly suppressed at both high gate and drain voltage. These results were verified by TCAD simulation.

articleTitle: Short-Loop Method to Shorten Gate Process Characterization Cycle Time
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: With CMOS device scaling down, process flow becomes more and more complicated and time-consuming. To shorten learning cycle is critical for technology development. Compared with full-loop method (from beginning to end through the wafer whole process flow), short-loop method (only a few parts of process steps) has the advantages of quicker feedback on Continuous Improvement Plan (CIP) conditions, as well as less resources (cost, manpower) needed. In this paper, we demonstrate the short-loop methodology to characterize Gate process, extracting electrical parameters such as Effective Work Function (eWF), Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT), which have direct impact on device performance.

articleTitle: Deep-Learning-Based Proxy Modeling for Microscopic Process of Plasma Etching
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Dynamic modeling of the microscopic process of plasma etching is crucial for reducing production costs and improving production efficiency. To alleviate issues such as poor real-time performance and limited transferability of typical numerical simulation algorithms, researchers have employed neural networks. Nonetheless, the considerable expenses often pose challenges in acquiring sufficient real datasets. Hence, this paper proposes the Deep-Learning-Based proxy model, combined with the Convolutional Autoencoder and Recurrent Neural Network. The model not only accelerates the simulation speed of plasma etching, but also achieves accurate predictions.

articleTitle: The Influence of Pin Position on CDM Peak Current of Chips Based on Large-Sized CoWoS Package
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This article mainly investigates the effect of pin position on the charged device model(CDM) peak current in CoWoS packaged chips. The results indicate that the peak current of CDM decreases significantly as the distance from the center increases for pins of the same type. The Power/Ground pin is mainly caused by a decrease in the quantity of electricity, while the IO pin is caused by an increase in the rise time of the first wave peak of the discharge.

articleTitle: UV-C Light Detection with High Performance Photodiodes Integrated in a $\mathbf{0.18}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$ Modular CMOS Foundry Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: To get a reliable detection of UV light, several issues must be solved. Impacting factors on the device and system level will be discussed. The paper starts with the material property aspects of silicon-based photodetectors, progresses to the device construction and readout to complement with the important aspect of reliability.

articleTitle: A New Fast XRD Apparatus for the Epitaxial Films with a Focusing X-Ray Beam
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: A new fast X-ray diffraction apparatus (ÅX-D100) for epitaxial (EPI) thin films has been developed with a convergent X-ray beam and a 2-D detector. The optic consists of an X-ray source of Cu-Target and a focusing capillary lens. The rocking curves (RC) for single crystals (GaAs, SiC, and InP) and epitaxial thin films (Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>As) were measured by using symmetric scanning method (Theta to theta scan). We also observed the periodic structure of superlattice layer stacks and calculated the Al composition, strain and density according to the RC of a Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>As epitaxial thin film. The experimental results indicated that the theta to theta scan mode of fast X-ray diffraction (XRD) device was appropriate for RC measurement and One-shoot mode could be used for in-line monitoring of the epitaxial films.

articleTitle: The Formation of Air Gaps Isolation Used in Metal/Dielectric Stacking
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Due to miniaturization of semiconductor devices, parasitic capacitors (C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P</inf>) in devices cause severe resistor capacitor (RC) delay. In order to reduce the C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P</inf> of the device, we use tunable plasma enhanced Tetraethyl Orthosilicate (PETEOS) to deposite silicon oxide (SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</inf>) within the trench between metal lines of each layer to form air gap structures. Thus, the C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P</inf> of devices can be greatly reduced and the RC delay can be optimized. Such process for forming air gap structures in metal/dielectric stacking shows great potential in reducing C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P</inf> for future DRAM development.

articleTitle: Mechanism Research and Improvement of AL Scratch Defect Based on MG CMP
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In the High-K Last process, MG CMP(Metal Gate Chemical Mechanical Planarization) is required to precisely control the height of the gate and the surface flatness. Defects such as scratches and AL residue may cause short circuits between metals. AL residue can usually be checked through the process window to debug the appropriate process conditions to solve, and scratch defect formation mechanism and possible related factors are many, need to be analyzed according to the actual situation. In this paper, the mechanism of MG CMP scratch is discussed in detail, the source of scratch is investigated according to the characteristics of scratch defects. The defects are improved from many influencing factors, including: CMP recipe optimization; Selection of pad and Conditioner; Optimization of mixing mode of slurry; The influence of Glue Layer thickness combination; Wafer surface especially wafer edge health check and optimization (The optimal result is to add the Wet bevel etch step).

articleTitle: Digitalization Solutions for Automated Material Handling Systems in Semiconductor Smart Factories
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Automated Material Handling Systems (AMHS) are an essential component of semiconductor smart factories. Traditional AMHS vendors focus mainly on transport management and path calculation based on automated handling equipment. To realize the digital transformation of modern semiconductor fabs, HIMC has introduced a comprehensive AMHS digital solution tailored to the semiconductor smart factories. In addition to Material Control System (MCS), Multiple OHT Controller (MOC) and subsystem control software, the solution also incorporates intelligent order dispatching and path optimization modules developed through algorithms and artificial intelligence technologies. Additionally, it employs digital twin technology, 3D rendering techniques, and big data analytics to achieve the real-time synchronization of the physical and digital worlds by converting two-dimensional data into three-dimensional visualizations. Through the implementation of these digitalization solutions, AMHS can achieve enhanced automation, efficiency, and sustainability, thereby improving the productivity and competitiveness of semiconductor smart factories.

articleTitle: A Study on SADP Film Stack Selection for Line Roughness Improvement in Planar 1Xnm NAND Flash
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: With planar NAND flash technology scaling down to reach 1xnm node, interference between cell has become the major factor for cycling and reliability degradation. Self-Aligned Double Patterning (SADP) approach has already been widely used to achieve the required complex structure of both AA and gate. Proper film stack selection can result in superior difference on physical structure and final performance. In this work, physical performance including CD bias, sidewall angle, line roughness and pitch walking are studied for different film stack selection. Further critical process tuning is also applied to optimize profile control and pattern loading by introducing extra process steps.

articleTitle: Evaluating 224G SI Performance of Vertical Interconnections on Package Substrate and PCB
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: 224G is the next generation SerDes technology to meet the data traffic demand in data center, and the standard groups of Ethernet and OIF are leading the creating of 224G PAM4 related specification. As the data rate is increased from 112Gbps PAM4 to 224Gbps PAM4, the signal Nyquist frequency will be doubled, increased from 28GHz to 56GHz, the channel bandwidth requirement will be increased too, maybe up to 84GHz(0.75*fb). As the 224G signal bandwidth increasing, the wavelength of the signal high frequency components can be comparable with the size of vertical interconnection structures in package(PKG) substrate and print circuit board (PCB), like the plated through hole(PTH) via and the stacked laser via in package substrate, the PTH via in PCB ball grid array (BGA) area and connector pin area. The high frequency characteristics of the electrical channel will be dominated by these vertical interconnection structures, like the channel bandwith(BW), the return loss(RL), the crosstalk, etc. This paper attempts to demonstrate the high frequency characteristics of vertical interconnections of the current 112G PAM4 design, and to explore the solutions to improve the high frequency performance of the vertical structures for the upcoming 224G PAM4 signaling, like the channel BW/IL/RL/erosstalk.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of CMOS Microbolometer With Metal-Insulator-Metal Absorbers
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, the Metal-Insulator-Metal-based (MIM) plasmonic metamaterial structure is designed to improve the detectivity of the CMOS microbolometer based on the standard technology. The MIM structure consists of three layers: Al/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Al and the materials used can be found in the integrated circuit process. Simulation results show that this MIM structure can effectively enhance the infrared absorption efficiency of microcalorimeter in the range of 7 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 13\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> Optical experiments on the fabricated device demonstrate that with the addition of MIM structure, the average detectivity (D*) of the microbolometer is increased by 52.13%, reaching <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.17\times 10^{9}$</tex> cm HZ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup>/W at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$9.8\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>. These performance improvements can make the microbolometer play a more important and stable role in medical diagnosis, environmental monitoring, security monitoring and so on.

articleTitle: A SelectiveNet-Based Method for Defect Classification in Semiconductor Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In semiconductor manufacturing, accurately classifying defects in scanning electron microscope (SEM) images is crucial for optimizing the production process. This paper introduces a novel defect classification frame-work based on SelectiveNet, which can reject predictions for defects with a high risk of misclassification through selective learning, effectively balancing the trade-offs between prediction coverage and accuracy for highly diverse and complex real SEM images. The efficacy of our proposed approach is demonstrated in the experiments with 95.14% classification accuracy with no reject and 98.37% at a selective learning coverage of 91.17% (rejection of 8.83%).

articleTitle: Hot-Carrier-Induced Degradations and Optimizations for Lateral DMOS Transistor with Shallow Trench Isolation and Step Oxide Improvement
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, hot carrier injection degradation in 80 V NLDMOS with shallow trench isolation (STI) is investigated and improved through STI corner rounding and thick STI oxide, step oxide and gate oxide optimization. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta \text{Idlin}$</tex> has different behavior with stress time at different conditions of Vgs (Isubmax and Vgmax). Combined with TCAD (Technology Computer Aided Design) simulation and experimental data, degradation mechanism was revealed. When the device is stressed under Vg (Isubmax), the hot electrons in the proximity of the accumulation region and source-side STI corner is the main cause of strong HCI degradation effects. For the device stressed under high Vgs (Vgmax), at first, drainside STI interface degradation by hot electrons is the major cause. Then with the increasing stress time, the drainside corner trap hot electrons and source-side STI oxide and step oxide trap hot holes, ultimately leading to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta \text{Idlin}$</tex> almost unchanged. Finally, only the hot electrons of drainside STI corner and drift region played a predominant role, resulting in that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta \text{Idlin}$</tex> revert to initial slope. Fortunately, it is concluded that STI corner rounding and thick STI oxide, step oxide and gate oxide are novel and effective method to optimize the HCI reliability according to combining with TCAD and experimental data.

articleTitle: Potential Confusion in the Analysis of the Current-Voltage Characteristics of High-K Dielectric on Lightly Doped P-Type Silicon MIS Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, the author will explain the potential confusion in the analysis of high-k MIS capacitor structures on lightly doped p-type silicon. The confusion comes from the possibility of the formation of an induced pn junction in lightly doped p-type silicon. Peripheral inversion and optical illumination can be important. An MISFET structure is a better test structure without such a problem.

articleTitle: Exploring the Effect of Gate Oxide Process on Electrical Performance of CMOS Device
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Based on the initial process flow conditions, this paper delves into an extensive exploration of the impact of key gate oxide process parameters, such as variations in Hydrogen content during oxidation and pressure during nitrogention, on the SiON layer thickness and nitrogen concentration. Subsequently, we investigate the influence of variations in these process parameters and the annealing method on the electrical properties of CMOS devices. This research is crucial for advancing the optimization of the gate oxide process to enhance the electrical performance of devices.

articleTitle: HBM Device Test & Repair Solution on T5833
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Nowadays, AI applications is booming developing, and it has had big progress at LLM. HBM, supplying the high-bandwidth and high-speed data solution in device, is supporting it behind the scenes. Compared to traditional DRAM, HBM structure is quite different with 3D-stacked at wafer process. The memory test on HBM is becoming crisscross complicated. To lower the complexity of the test HBM should also some optimized designs. Advantest's T5833, is a key memory tester, which has a full solution on the memory repair. Combined with the ALPG and DBM, it could handle all requirements of HBM test.

articleTitle: Advances and Reliability Challenges in Heterogeneous Integration in Chiplet ERA: From Solder to Copper to Optical Interconnects
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Advanced packaging is adopting more and more Cu-based interconnects in addition to conventional solder-based bumps, including micro-bumps (Cu pillars with solder caps), TSVs, Cu-Cu hybrid bonding, RDLs and Si bridges for lateral interconnects. Optical interconnects are also gaining traction. Heterogeneous integration of multiple chips into a package with these advanced interconnects and different materials poses difficult reliability challenges. This paper discusses the recent advances in the interconnect technologies with a focus on their reliability performance.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Technologies for Semiconductor Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: As the size of semiconductor devices decreases and the structures and materials become increasingly complex, manufacturing these devices is becoming more difficult. The complexity of IC research and development (R&D) and the scale of high-volume manufacturing (HVM) have greatly increased the cost and time required to reach final production. Chipmakers, equipment manufacturers and software companies are exploring and deploying machine learning (ML) technology in a wide range of applications, including process development, production maintenance, metrology, and yield improvement, to address these scale-up issues. With more than a decade of expertise deploying ML technology for semiconductor manufacturing, Lam Research has developed several smart tools and ML solutions to optimize quality, efficiency, and productivity and accelerate innovation in semiconductor manufacturing. In this paper, two of Lam's smart tools — SEMulator3D® and Equipment Intelligence® Data Analyzer (EI-DA) —are introduced to demonstrate how Lam's advanced technology can be used to efficiently manufacture state-of-the-art microchips during R&D and HVM.
