articleTitle: Incoming Impact on Dishing Improvement in FEOL Process
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The dishing improvement always is the eternal goal of Chemical Mechanical Planarization (CMP). A lot of reports about dishing improvement come from CMP itself, such as adjustments of polish pressure, flow rate, rotate speed, slurry selective ratio etc. However, the study of incoming impact on dishing has been reported rarely. In this paper, it has been shown that we can do something in incoming layers for dishing improvement. The dishing could be effectively decreased by adding ion implantation process, UV cure process, setting different anneal temperature in incoming films or introducing the extra layers which polish rate lower than target layer.

articleTitle: A Universal DPAT GUI Solution for Production Test
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, we have addressed a universal DPAT GUI solution for ATE production test based on V93K SMT8 environment. The basic method follows closely to Automotive Electronics Council document AEC-Q001. User can set the numbers of the devices used for estimating the mean and standard deviation. Using these estimates, dynamic PAT limits for the batch are applied for further test. An embedded GUI tool helps speed up the development of production test program. With this solution, DPAT test can be precisely and easily applied to guarantee the zero-defect requirements for automotive testing with the best Time-to-Market.

articleTitle: The Influence of Metal Barrier Punch Through Process on Dielectric Reliability at 55 nm CMOS Node
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The influence of metal barrier punch through process on electrical property, dielectric reliability and failure mechanism is investigated for copper (Cu) interconnect with TaN/Ta metal barrier layers, using via first (VF) and trench first (TF) dual damascene (DD) process. It is found that with improved cross-section profiles, the optimized integrations show not only smaller via/line resistances due to the reduction of barrier thickness, but also an improvement in breakdown voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">bd</inf>) by preventing Cu from penetrating into the dielectric layer at the line bottom, and thus enhancing the reliability of interlevel dielectric layers.

articleTitle: Innovated Methodology Improving CD Uniformity for Lithography Using Wafer-Less Dynamic Grouping Process Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This paper has proposed an intelligent methodology for inline high volume manufacturing (HVM), initiated by complexity of mature logic foundries. To improve on-product lithography performance, e.g. CD, Overlay, the conventional operation is to generate the compensation with intra-field and inter-field metrology result of real production wafer in process, which resulted in cost and cycle time loss. Logic foundries will have different product/process requirements which are having quite diversified process characteristics, causing intensive on-wafer-metrology and process correction setup accordingly. How to establish a flexible group/tracking/control system can increase ramping phase and improve yield within very limited cycle time is an universal challenge for years. We have initiated an inline control system, forecast the process variations with the main contributors without processed wafer and correct in advance. Such as to improve inline CDU performance, correct the hybrid intra-field and inter-field fingerprint which were estimated with mask CD and process characteristics. Also combined with context information from process model other than lithography as grouping index database, which is trackable indicator used as Run-to-Run (R2R) tuning parameters.

articleTitle: Design and Experiment of a Micro Planar Linear Motor Equipped with Electromagnetic Guide
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, the design and experiment of a planar linear motor equipped with an integrated electromagnetic guide is proposed. The motor consists of a stator and a mover. The stator has a novel design which integrates a driving coil with a guide micro coil into one chip. The mover has a line/space permanent magnet structure. The working principle of the motor, the motor configuration and the electromagnetic force performance is analyzed. The motor prototype is fabricated by micro micromachining process. The motor is experimentally evaluated, the slider attained a maximum velocity of 50mm/s with stable attachable performance. Furthermore, the electromagnetic guide enables adjustable stiffness as well as enlarge the mover bandwidth.

articleTitle: Newly Developed Low-Reflectivity Black Resist with High Optical Density
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The black resist has been generally used in a various kind of devices such as displays and CMOS sensors. To improve the device performance, it was required to have high light shielding properties, low reflectance, and high lithographic performance. Furthermore, in recent years, the number of Infra-red (IR) sensor devices had increased, such as time of flight (TOF) sensors, which was required not only for visible light but also for the IR region having shielding layer for both high light-shielding and low-reflective properties. So far, it was difficult to satisfy all these properties, however, newly developed black resist could be achieved all those properties by modifying black materials and the resin components. The resist could be exposed by i-line lithography and compatible with conventional aqueous alkaline development. The resist reflectance was possible to achieve a reflectance below 2% from the visible region to the IR wavelength range. Both 200 µm line & space and 50 µm hole patterns were demonstrated with the newly developed black resist formulation.

articleTitle: First Principle Study on Oxygen Vacancy Induced Ferroelectricity in HFO2-Based Ferroelectrics
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> have attracted much research interest because of its wide application in beyond-moore computing based on the fantastic effects observed in the HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-based devices such as resistive switching and ferroelectricity. However, the physical mechanism of ferroelectricity remains elusive. Based on first principle calculations, we propose a new mechanism on the ferroelectricity in HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, in which the oxygen vacancies can induce ferroelectricity through symmetry-breaking mechanism. Using first principle methods, we found a stable monoclinic-like ferroelectric M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> phase with oxygen vacancies in sub-stoichiometric Hf<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>Zr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2-δ</inf> system and studied its ferroelectric properties. Our proposed mechanism may provide a new way for characterization and optimization of HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-based devices.

articleTitle: Two-Dimensional MOS2 Based Memristors for Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Neuromorphic computing has recently gained significant research interest due to its potential for efficient computing enabled by dense integration of memristive devices. However, few studies have demonstrated neurons and synapses utilizing the same two-dimensional (2D) materials and fabrication process. In this work, we investigate molybdenum disulfide (MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) treated with thermal oxidation as both volatile memristors (VMs) and non-volatile memristors (NVMs) for neuromorphic applications. For the VM, the devices with the structure of Ag/Ti/MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2-x</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>/Pt devices exhibit low operation voltages, low-variability in threshold voltage. The structure of Pt/Ti/MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2-x</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>/Pt demonstrates gradual set and reset behavior mimicking synaptic plasticity.

articleTitle: Study of Coating Effect on TEM Sample Damage and Elemental Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Electron beam induced film deposition has been found to be an effective method to protect the sample surface for both Focused Ion Beam (FIB) and Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) analysis. It's known that the sample damage caused by low voltage electron beam assisted deposition should be nearly negligible while dealing with electron beam sensitive or temperature sensitive materials. Adhesive coating is also generally considered as an alternative to electron beam deposition, as a protective layer which minimizes the sample damage. However, samples prepared using low-voltage electron beam induced deposition are considered to be more favorable for X-ray Energy Dispersive Spectroscopy (EDS) elemental analysis than ones prepared using adhesive coating. Important to note, that discussed in this paper conductive layer as a protection layer that doesn't cause physical damage, shows a good S/N (Signal to Noise) ratio for element analysis.

articleTitle: Fabrication Process Improvement of Aggressively Scaled Dual-Bit/Cell Split-Gate Floating-Gate Flash Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: A novel method was proposed to optimize the fabrication process of the aggressively scaled non self-aligned split-gate floating-gate (FG) NOR-type Dual-bit/cell (NORD) flash cell. The improvement method solved the issue of the overlay shift between two times of lithography, which results in the asymmetry FG and control gate (CG) between the two bits in one cell. The cell well implant and lightly doped drain (LDD) implant have been modified to make sure the device performance can match that of conventional cell. The technology computer-aided-design (TCAD) simulation results suggest that the changes in gate lengths don't cause declines in device characteristics and even better performance in readout window and program efficiency, which confirms the feasibility of the fabrication process improvement method.

articleTitle: An Intelligent General-Purpose Circuit and System for Broad Sensor Array-Based Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Here, we present a general-purpose sensor array-based circuit and system design. Firstly, to reduce power consumption and suppress noises, we introduce strategies including multiple bias voltages, low-power self-wake-up mechanism, average-lag filtering and data packetization mechanisms. Then, we implement hardware-friendly algorithms: 1) for the novel strain sensor array, KNN algorithm affiliated with the threshold discrimination mechanism successfully recognizes ten kinds of gestures for deaf and mute person with an accuracy of 99.8%; 2) for the MEMS gas sensor array, combined with the adaptive mean-baseline calibration algorithm, we successfully compensate common problems of the drift.

articleTitle: Study on ELK Dielectric Reliability During the Solder Reflow Process Based on Finite Element Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: As device dimensions shrink, the use of ELK dielectric becomes crucial for reducing interline capacitance and RC delay. However, ELK dielectric materials are susceptible to mechanical stress, leading to potential cracks. CPI, resulting from CTE mismatch between die and substrate, can introduce thermal load directly onto ELK layers and cause crack formation and propagation. In this paper, the finite element simulation method is applied to investigate ELK layer stress during the cooling stage of the solder reflow process. Impacts of various parameters on ELK layer stress are analyzed. The results indicate that the mechanical properties of bump solder have a significant impact on the local stress of ELK layer. Additionally, the height of bump solder cap, bump pitch and the thickness of PI layer are also assessed as variables influencing the ELK layer stress. After the parameter optimization, the maximum value of the equivalent plastic strain of solder and the tensile stress of ELK dielectric layer are effectively reduced by 34% and 40% respectively.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Three-Side-Around Control Gate of Semi-Floating Gate Transistor
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Semi-floating gate (SFG) transistor is a novel dynamic random access memory (DRAM), which uses an embedded tunneling field-effect (TFET) transistor for charging and discharging the semi-floating gate. The charging efficiency is constrained by the relatively small capacitance due to traditional limited coupling area between control gate and semi-floating gate. In this paper, we report a novel method to fabricate 3D semi-floating gate transistor with three-side-around control gate. Poly cut approach is applied to isolate semi-floating gate and offer additional area (∼66%) for coupling control gate. The increasing capacitance could trap more charges and lead to more obvious difference to the transistor threshold voltage (VT). With the same Read 0 current, the Read 1 current is 6.7 times higher than that of traditional semi-floating gate device. This design provides a technical scheme for further boosting semi-floating gate transistor.

articleTitle: Improvement of Line Roughness of Fin by Conventional Thermal Oxidation and Atomic Level Low-Temperature Ozone Treatments
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, conventional thermal oxidation (CTO) and atomic level low-temperature ozone (LTO) treatment were utilized to successfully thin the width of fin and reduce the surface roughness. Meanwhile, the line edge roughness (LER) and line width roughness (LWR) of fin were compared under the two schemes. The result show that after three sacrificial oxidizations and DHF rinsing, the LER and LWR of fins were reduced by 40.1% (from 4.64 nm to 2.78 nm) and 55.5% (from 2.38 nm to 1.06 nm), respectively. In addition, after 12 cycles of LTO and HF rinsing, the LER and LWR of fin decreased by 67.4% (from 4.30 nm to 1.40 nm) and 61.3% (from 2.66 nm to 1.03 nm), respectively. And, the cross-correlation coefficients (ρ) were 0.92 and 0.72, respectively. The result provide a guidance for channel surface optimization and low-temperature integration of FinFET devices at advanced technology nodes.

articleTitle: The Effects of Different Silicon Oxide Substrates on Amorphous Silicon Thin-Film
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, the influences of different substrates on the performance of amorphous silicon (a-Si) film including thickness, within-wafer uniformity, and roughness were studied. The a-Si films were prepared on three different silicon oxide substrates (Dry Oxide, Wet Oxide and HCl Oxide) under three seeding time split conditions. The results showed that the a-Si deposited on wet oxide substrate presented the thickest film, the best uniformity, and the best roughness in all spilt conditions. The presence of a large number of-OH on wet oxide substrate provide dense and uniform nucleation sites which increase the whole growth rate and reduce the difference of growth rate between different areas. Furthermore, the uniform nucleation sites led to the uniform size of the nucleus, and further obtained good roughness in the continuous films. The addition of seeding significantly optimized the performance of a-Si film, and the a-Si deposited on wet oxide substrate still showed the best uniformity and roughness compared to the other two substrates.

articleTitle: Effect of Surfactants on CMP Properties of C-, A- and R-Plane Sapphire
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Sapphire is widely used in many fields such as optics and integrated circuits, and these applications require increasingly high surface quality and polishing efficiency. Chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) technology is currently the only process technology to achieve global planarization of sapphire. Slurry is one of the key factors affecting the performance of CMP, and changes in its composition can greatly affect the polishing quality. Therefore, in this article the effects of two surfactants (JFCE and CDEA) on the material removal rate (MRR) and surface roughness of C-, A- and R-plane sapphire surfaces were investigated. The results indicate that both surfactants can improve the MRR and surface quality of sapphire. JFCE is slightly better than CDEA in the same condition.

articleTitle: A 16-Bit 8MSPS SAR ADC with a Configurable Low-Power Comparator
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This paper demonstrates a 16-bit 8MSPS successive approximation register (SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC) with a configurable low-power comparator. Based on bottom plate sampling and bootstrap switch, this SAR ADC adopts segmented capacitive DAC arrays and a dynamic SAR control logic, with a proposed configurable comparator to lower power consumption. This proposed SAR ADC is designed and simulated in a 0.18-um BCD process, whose power consumption is reduced by 10.12% compared with the traditional structures while achieving 14.07 ENOB at 8MSPS sampling rate.

articleTitle: Characterization of ALD Low-K Films
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Silicon nitride (SiN) has long been chosen for the MOSFET sidewall spacers owing to its exceptional blocking capabilities, insulating properties, thermal stability, and resistance to hydrofluoric acid. As the device is continually scaling down, the parasitic capacitance stemming from the gate and contact continues escalating. It can impact the signal stability. Silicon oxycarbonnitride (SiOCN) material emerges as a promising substitute for SiN, presenting advantages such as ease of processing and a favorable low dielectric constant (K). This paper aims to study properties of SiOCN films grown by atomic layer deposition (ALD).

articleTitle: Design of Arbitrarily Polarized CMOS Terahertz Detector Based on Plasmonic Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this work, an innovative arbitrarily polarized (AP) THz detector with the assembling of the orthogonally crossed silicon-based plasmonic antenna and the symmetrical MOSFET in one compact unit is proposed and fabricated in standard CMOS technology. The plasmonic antenna is designed as a dual orthogonal structure with both bow-tie and rod characteristics. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed detector exhibits excellent polarization insensitivity with an axial ratio of 1.3 dB, furthermore, the noise equivalent power (NEP) and responsivity (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{v}$</tex>) of the detector are about 60.25 pW/Hz and 1.3 kV/W, while the area occupied is only 180 µm x 180 µm, The presented AP detector offers a novel approach for THz high-density and high-performance array integration.

articleTitle: Sn-Ag Compatible Selective Ti Etch in Cu RDL Fabrication and 3D IC Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Selective Titanium (Ti) etch chemistries have been developed to provide enabling Ti removal up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.2\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> thickness with good Cu, Sn-Ag and TEOS compatibility. They are alkaline oxidizing compositions with unique etch promoters. Their applications in Cu RDL and 2.5D/3D integrations have been demonstrated. Etch mechanisms and substrate compatibility are also discussed.

articleTitle: A Closed-Loop Chip Fast Binning Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Binning is one of the effective techniques to improve chip yield. However, with the increase of IC complexity and the exponential growth of test vectors, the traditional binning method has to face the drawbacks of high testing difficulty and low efficiency, as well as the problem of not being able to quickly differentiate the test results of numerous blocks. In order to solve the above problems and make faults more efficiently detected&recorded, this paper proposes a closed-loop chip fast binning technology, which provides an innovative test circuit structure and fault detect&record method for MBIST and SCAN tests.

articleTitle: An optimized ADC&DAC test solution from SmartScale MCx to ExaScale WSMX
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This paper introduce a 12-site ADC&DAC test solution with WSMX based on ExaScale platform which replace the 4-site test solution with MCx based on SmartScale. The main challenges of the solution include I. the complex hardware design which realize higher parallelism test with limited board resources. II. Replace the original MCx LF&VHF unit with WSMX HS unit. The specs differences between the two analog cards including sampling rate, bandwidth, noise floor, and resolution bring challenges to program development and correlation. Especially with WSMX HS unit substitute MCx LF unit. III. Differences in the use method of PS5000+WSMX instead of PS1600+MCx. Based on these challenges, this paper puts forward a series of solutions, including I. with fanout technology and multilevel relay to achieve 312 analog port test covered by 1xWSMX card. II. A software-based algorithm is proposed to achieve a sampling rate lower than the WSMX HS hardware spec for signal sampling. And the frequency band response characteristics of the digital filtering algorithm are analyzed, and used to compensate the bandwidth difference between WSMX HS Unit and MCx LF Unit, and finally achieving the static test results consistency between WSMX HS Unit and MCx LF Unit under the same test conditions. At the same time, the noise floor difference between WSMX HS unit in ExaScale and MCx VHF unit in SmartScale is analyzed, optimizing the sampling rate settings and achieving the dynamic test results consistency between WSMX HS unit and MCx VHF unit. III. This paper studies the different trigger response characteristics between WSMX HS Unit and MCx LF&VHF unit, thus optimize PS5000 trigger set up. Finally, this paper successfully developed a 12-site ADC&DAC test solution with 1xWSMX on the ExaScale platform which upgrade the original 4-site test solution.

articleTitle: Heat Transfer Improvement of Phase Change Material With Metal Foam
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Temperature control is essential to the stable performance and lifetime of electronic products. Phase change materials can absorb the heat generated by electronic components or devices and keep the product's temperature steady during the phase change process. However, the low thermal conductive properties limit their applications in the thermal management of high density electronics. Metal foams are used as thermal conductive enhancer to improve the heat transfer of paraffin wax in this paper. The effective thermal conductivities and heat transfer features of composite are investigated by numerical simulation. Various structures and materials of metal foams are taken into consideration, and the phase change characteristics are studied.

articleTitle: An Efficient Protocol ATE Solution for Driver IC on Advantest T6391
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: At present, people's demand for visual perception is constantly increasing, the data transmission rate and the number of source driver pins of the DDIC are developing in the direction of faster and more, and the data transmission protocol is becoming more diversified with different application scenarios, such as USI/ISP /MIPI, etc. These technological and product changes have put forward higher requirements and adjustments for the automatic test of DDIC. Faced with the diversity of transport protocols, this paper provides an efficient GPIPG (General Procotol interface Pattern Generator) solution for all protocol-related test patterns on T639l, to meet the test demand of the next generation DDIC. This solution can easily generate test patterns and get corresponding test program, reduce engineers' human resources and program development time, and thus achieve the purpose of cost reduction.

articleTitle: Mask Corner Rounding in OPC Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The continued development of semiconductor manufacturing technology and the pressing demand for the accuracy and predictability of lithography simulators, it becomes increasingly important to understand actual mask condition. This paper aims to identify an effective and efficient method to model mask corner rounding (MCR) in computational lithography. First, we have found that Gaussian function can be used as a good convolution kernel for mask, which can represent the MCR, and we have found a good corresponding relationship. Second, we propose a modeling flow which integrates the MCR effect and optical simulation framework, and we have found that it seems to perform quite well.

articleTitle: Anomalous Hot Carrier Injection Induced Degradation of Drain Current in High-Voltage NMOS with Shallow Trench Isolation
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In 25V High-Voltage NMOS manufactured by 28nm High-K Metal Gate (HKMG) process, the first peak of Isub appears at Vg=6.7V. Due to the hot carrier injection (HCI, stress condition @Vg=6.7V, Vd=27.5V), the linear current Idlin (Vd=0.05V) firstly increases and then decreases with time when the gate voltage Vg is low (<4V), and Idlin monotonously decreases when Vg is high (>4V), which is different from previous research. Under a certain stress time, the degradation of drain current (Vg=25V) is the largest when Vd=4.5V. Two competing mechanisms were proposed to explain the maximum degradation at Vd=4.5V. The mechanisms above were confirmed utilizing TCAD simulation and were integrated in manufacturing process. The obtained results confirmed the presume and helped to study and improve the HCI reliability.

articleTitle: Study of Improvement for Substrate Current in High-Voltage NMOS with Shallow Trench Isolation
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Hot carrier injection (HCI) effect is closely related to substrate current (Isub). In 25V High-Voltage NMOS, the Isub-Vg by substrate bias curve is studied and two peaks, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Isub}_{\max}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{I}_{\text{kirk}}$</tex> are observed. Due to the inevitable Kirk effect, the process of Kirk effect in parasitic n+pn-n+ bipolar transistor is studied. A formula is proposed, which plays a guide line for the later research. When substrate bias is higher, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Isub}_{\max}$</tex> is smaller, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{I}_{\text{kirk}}$</tex> is larger and Isub<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> appears later. The drain current Id-Vg (Vd=25V) curve in the saturation region is also tested, which exhibits obvious velocity saturation effect. In addition, the influence of process and device size parameters on Isub is studied, and the reasons are analyzed, which is helpful to promote the research of Isub and HCI.

articleTitle: Ultrathin TIO2 Channel HfLaO FeFET with Low Operation Voltage
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: An ultrathin metal-ferroelectric-semiconductor (MFS) structured ferroelectric field effect transistor (F eFET) with a TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> channel and HfLaO ferroelectric (FE) layer is reported for low voltage operation capability. The 8 nm HfLaO and 6 nm TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> layers were continuously deposited by in-situ atomic layer deposition (ALD). Reasonable memory characteristics and low voltage operation capabilities, including 15 µC/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> remnant polarization (Pi), 0.9 V coercive voltage (Vc) and 1.28 V memory window (MW) are demonstrated in the fabricated ultrathin FeFETs.

articleTitle: Integration of Shift-Left Updates into Logic Synthesis and Macro Placement
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The shift left methodology in Electronic Design Automation (EDA) presents a pathway for the creation of digital twins, facilitating the transition of subsequent physically-aware design processes into virtual environments. This shift empowers designers to establish stronger correlations and optimize their designs more effectively. However, it is crucial to identify when and how to implement this shift, especially considering the challenges in replicating subsequent behaviors accurately. Given that synthesis marks the initiation of the entire physical implementation phase, and macro placement serves as the starting point for intensive automated placement, we have pinpointed opportunities to introduce shift left updates to these critical stages. By incorporating a physically aware timing model into logic synthesis, we have significantly enhanced design quality in terms of timing. Additionally, by preemptively considering macro-cell connections as a co-optimization target, Improvements have been observed in routing length and congestion, leading to more efficient designs.

articleTitle: Data Flow Graph Partitioning Method for CGRA Temporal Mapping Based on Bayesian Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Coarse-Grained Reconfigurable Arrays (CGRAs) are attracting more and more attention for their high flexibility and energy efficiency. Due to the limited resources, mapping large data flow graphs (DFGs) that represent application kernels onto a CGRA is difficult, for which partitioning is employed. However, existing partitioning methods in the CGRA domain are unable to solve large kernels. In this work, we propose BOPart, an efficient DFG partitioning method based on Bayesian optimization. This enables the mapping of large DFGs that surpass the capacity of the target CGRA. Moreover, we design a graph coarsening method to reduce the complexity of the partitioning problem, which further improves the performance and convergence of BOPart. BOPart can handle benchmarks with up to 333 operations, surpassing the capability of state-of-the-art temporal mapping and partitioning method, which can only handle benchmarks with up to 94 operations.

articleTitle: A Graphene Field Effect Transistor (GFET) Based Integrated Biosensor System for Point-of-Care Application
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: An electronic Point-Of-Care (POC) system for early-stage disease detection with wide detection range, ultralow detection limit and high detection speed is strongly desired. The novel POC system satisfying the aforementioned criterial requires both innovative detection device as well as a sensitive readout system. Here we designed and fabricated an ASIC system including graphene field effect transistor (GFET) bio-electronic sensor chip as well as corresponding sensitive readout system. The GFET is ultra-sensitive due to monolayer nature of its 2D channel, and the readout system is able to collect> 100 data points per second with 0.5 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{A}$</tex> current resolution and 1 m V voltage resolution. The entire POC system enable ultralow limit detection of hsa-miR-125b within minutes, a major breakthrough for Alzheimer's disease detection.

articleTitle: Investigation of Electrical Characteristics of a Fabricated Lgad Detectors at High and Low Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The High Granularity Time Detector (HGTD) project need advanced Low-Gain Avalanche Detector (LGAD) for constructing the timing precision layer in the ATLAS detector. It undergoes a strong environmental temperature impact for cooling the absorbed high-energy particles. In this paper, an investigation of the manufacturing process of LGAD detectors and their characteristics in terms of dark current and breakdown voltage at high and low temperatures are systematical explored. The behavior of carrier transport within the device at various temperature conditions was analyzed using TCAD simulation tools.

articleTitle: A New Multi-Mode X-Ray Fluorescence Apparatus for Both Blanket and Pattern Wafer Film Metrology
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Åx-t110, a new X-ray fluorescence (XRF) apparatus, combining two optics systems, has been developed to offer a high-throughput metrology solution with good repeatability and the capability to address inline metrology challenges. Depending on its application, its throughput can be up to 80 WPH (wafers per hour, 5 sites per wafer) with a dynamic precision of less than 0.17% (1 sigma). Moreover, its specially designed micro spot optics enable it to measure pattern wafers, making it a great complementary approach to optical spectroscopy technology when facing metallic film metrology challenges. In this paper, we introduce the main configuration of this apparatus. Additionally, certain application cases are discussed to demonstrate its capabilities.

articleTitle: Novel Etch Solution with SYM3® for Logic Beol Patterning Etch Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: With technology node shrinks in logic / foundry, patterning etch and Titanium Nitride (TiN) Hard Mask Open (HMO) are facing increasing challenges on on-wafer performance and productivity control to ensure device performance and yield. Applied Materials' etch product Sym3® is developed to address such challenges with unique chamber design and innovative features via uniformity tuning, etch profile and selectivity control, process window expansion, and defectivity control. Till date >10000 chambers have been deployed in logic and memories fabs and are production-proven as leading solution for patterning and TiN HMO etch.

articleTitle: A Study on Cross-Level Interconnection of Metal Layers Under 193 Immersion Lithography Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In advanced integrated circuit manufacturing technology, equipment, materials, and processes are continually improved to meet the requirement for smaller and more efficient chips. Lithography, a crucial step in chip manufacturing, requires continuous research and development. Metal layers, serving as the interconnect layers, usually have very complex patterns. This is because there are usually many metal and via layers, which takes a big fraction of the total manufacturing cost. Hence, If we can reduce the number of metal and via masks, the manufacturing cost may be significantly reduced. By accommodating more complex patterns in the metal layers, we may save more mask area and thereby reduce the number of masks. This paper will focus on the study of the cross-level interconnection patterns that may appear in the Back-End-Of-the-Line (BEOL) metal layers at 14 nm and 7 nm through simulation with self-developed tool based on Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) algorithm.

articleTitle: Two Step Etching Method for Removing Thick Photoresist
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Strip is an important process after etching is completed, and if it is not removed thoroughly, defects will form and have a serious impact on the subsequent process. This article introduces a two-step method for removing thick photoresist. Complete the removal of thick photoresist by adding steps containing H2 gas.

articleTitle: Virtual FAB Semiconductor Process Modeling Augmented Vertical Gate All Around Complementary FET Based 6T SRAM Path-Finding
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Vertical Gate All Around Nanowire Complementary FET based logic circuits offer an alternative way for higher cell density without aggressive gate length scaling. In this study, we develop a device to circuit design-technology co-optimization (DTCO) flow that incorporates Virtual Fab Semiconductor Process Modeling and physics-based TCAD simulations. We compare VGAA Complementary FET (CFET) based 6T SRAM with its counterparts by conventional planar CMOS, sequential/monolithic 3DIC CFETs with lateral transistors, accounting for the parasitics from virtual fab modeling. Our results show that VGAA CFETs offer better control over the channel and reduce parasitic capacitances and resistances compared to the counterpart technology options.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Automatic Test Pattern Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Automatic test pattern generation (ATPG) is a key technology in digital circuit testing. In this paper, we propose an ATPG method based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL), aiming to reduce the backtracking of ATPG and thereby improve its performance. Specifically, we apply deep Q-network (DQN) in reinforcement learning to the PODEM (path-oriented decision making) ATPG algorithm, and design a reward function to maximize cumulative rewards through continuous interactions with the circuit. Such a design can enable the DRL agent to learn the optimal policy to guide backtracing decisions within PODEM. Experimental results show that the proposed method can perform better than traditional and artificial neural network (ANN)- based heuristic strategies on most benchmark circuits.

articleTitle: A Novel Ultralow Voltage Slope Device
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Novel device architectures based on oxide materials have overcome the fundamental thermionic limit of the switching slope (60 mV/ dec). However, a versatile switching device required for highly integrated memory and neuromorphic applications has not been achieved with such exceptional switching slope characteristics. Here, we demonstrate a record-low switching voltage slope down to 0.221 mV/dec in a threshold switching device based on the novel du-al-layer oxide stacked structure, and the threshold voltage of the device can be as low as 0.177V.

articleTitle: The Influence of Different Parameters on Capacitive Coupled Magnetron Sputtering Process
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, experiments were carried out in a physical vapor deposition (PVD) chamber with DC magnetron and substrate RF system. With RF power increasing, it was found that film thickness gradually decreased and the thickness uniformity was maintained at a stable level. With the increase of dep time, the thickness increased and thickness uniformity was improved, while the overall sheet resistance (Rs) was stable at a level and the Rs uniformity gradually decreases. With the decrease of process position, the thickness of the deposited film decreased and thickness uniformity became better, while the Rs trended up and Rs uniformity trended down. This paper confirms the effect of RF power, dep time and H-T-Spacing on process, which is important for industrial development of wafer processes.

articleTitle: Study on 28NM Technology Node ILD0-CMP Micro_Scratch Defect Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: With the rapid development of IC (Integrated Circuit) devices, defects which come from CMP (Chemical Mechanical Planarization) process including dishing, residue and scratch have become inconvenient yield detractors. As the expansion of application scenarios, many ideas of characteristic 28nm HK (high-k) metal gate (MG) technology have been put forward, in which 28HKL+ with unique N/P work function split presents an important challenge to us. In order to optimize 28HKL+ ILD0 (Zero Inter Layer Dielectric)-CMP dishing, the hard oxide is selected as dielectric film, which is different from other 28HK products. However, the unexpected seesaw effect appeared between slight dishing and worse micro_scratch in 28HKL+ ILD0-CMP process. In this work, a novel approach has been developed to tackle this challenge, which can reduce micro_scratch ∼70% without influencing the good dishing performance. This work not only solves the yield killer and promotes the development of 28HKL+, but also provides a new perspective for solving micro_scratch in FEOL (front end of line) CMP.

articleTitle: A Study of Deep Hole Etching In Mo&Dielectric Alterning Multilayer Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Molybdenum(Mo) is suitable for gate and inter-connection materials in integrated semiconductor with high melting point and low resistance. In this paper, we studied the inductively coupled plasma (ICP) of deep hole in Mo and dielectric multilayers structure. articleTitle: Ultra-Deep via Etching of Silicon Oxide for High-Voltage Capacitive Isolators
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: High-voltage capacitive isolators typically use SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> as the dielectric layer, and the required thickness of silicon oxide is generally large. However, as the size of the pattern in the integrated circuit decreases, the thickness of the intermetallic dielectric layer decreases accordingly, resulting in the cumulative thickness of all the intermetallic dielectric layers having difficulty in meeting the requirement. In order to achieve the high-voltage withstand target, we added an extra dielectric layer above the top metal layer, but this method increased the difficulty of silicon oxide etching. In this study, we investigated the effects of etching conditions, such as mask material, mask thickness, and etching process parameters on ultra-deep via etching of silicon oxide, and obtained a single maximum etching depth of 8 um for silicon oxide.

articleTitle: PMOS Leakage Reduction Through Sige Morphology & IMP Profile Fine Tune
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In the pursuit of reducing the leakage of PMOS, this research investigates methods to enhance the performance of PMOS devices through an analysis of halo dose and SiGe morphology. Experimental results highlight the critical influence of halo dose on device performance, with higher doses leading to improved outcomes. Additionally, a correlation is established between halo depth and SiGe morphology, influencing device characteristics. By precisely adjusting the Ge injection energy, the thickness of the amorphous layer can be finely controlled, facilitating optimal matching between halo depth and SiGe morphology. Notably, experimental investigations reveal significant performance improvements resulting from the optimization of halo dose and SiGe morphology. This study provides valuable insights for enhancing PMOS devices incorporating SiGe and offers practical guidance for effective online control during large-scale production processes.

articleTitle: Virtual Measurement Combine OCD and FDC Through Optimized Random Forest Machine Learning Algorithm Assists on Post Etching Monitor
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Etching is an important process in semiconductor technology. Inconsistency in post Etching wafer uniformity and geometry affects downstream process margin which leads to various yield issues. Post etching monitor such as top, middle or bottom critical dimension is necessary to ensure the process meet the specification and stability. Wafer geometry will be measured and out of control wafers will be reworked or Scraped. To reduce rework and scraped, Etching is normally employed with process control systems like APC (Advanced process Control). The Operation of APC usually relies on conventional measurement methods such as CDSEM or Optical Critical Dimension(OCD) for Feedback or Feedforward. Conventional metrology tools are in charge of ensuring the data quality for APC which need huge sampling data but challenged by the limitation of time and cost. Fault Detection and Classification (FDC) data reflects machine real time status that provide information for diagnosing process quality. However, the selection of FDC parameters is very dependent on the engineering experience, thus it can only be used as an auxiliary means of monitor. In this paper, we combine the traditional OCD measurement with the real-time FDC data of Etching chamber to establish the machine learning prediction model by training the optimized random forest algorithm and carried out virtual measurement finally.

articleTitle: Breakthrough the Test Challenges for the Latest BeiDou Navigation and Satellite Communications Chips
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: BeiDou navigation and short message communication technologies have faded into people's sight in recent years. It is a new application that could support mobiles to “break through the sky” and communicate with BeiDou satellites, enabling users to send short messages even if no cellular signal exists. With the rapid development of the BeiDou-3 short message business in the consumer market, the BeiDou-3 navigation and short message communication device (the device) will be massively applied in mobile terminals. The Automatic test solution is needed to meet high-volume production test requirements. This paper introduces an automatic test solution for an actual BeiDou communication device on the V93000 platform. This device is a core component of the BeiDou communication system, it is usually packaged using WLCSP and needs some special test coverages. This paper will talk about the critical test challenges of these chips, how V93000 breaks through 、 these challenges, and achieving high throughput and cost-effective test solutions.

articleTitle: Investigation of Self-Heating Effect on Forksheet Field-Effect Transistors
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: As a candidate device for a 3nm node, due to the presence of dielectric wall in the device, Forksheet Field Effect Transistors (FSFETs) have more severe self-heating and thermal crosstalk than ordinary Complementary FET (CFET). The impacts of related geometric shape and nanosheet size of dielectric walls are presented, providing guidance for self-heating effects (SHE) in device design. A thermal network model for Forksheet devices is proposed to quickly evaluate temperature changes under AC conditions. The results indicate that high attention should be paid to the self-heating of Forksheet devices.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Carrier Velocity in Short Channel Ge MOSFET with NiGe Metal Source/Drain
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Schottky barrier MOSFETs have attracted attention as a candidate for achieving high-performance MOSFETs. In the short channel MOSFETs with metal source/drain, the velocity overshoot phenomenon exists. In this article, we analyze the carrier velocity in the short-channel Ge pMOSFETs with metal source/drain. The velocity overshoot phenomenon becomes more obvious with the decrease in channel length. At the same time, it is also shown that with the same channel length, the relationship of carrier velocity and vertical electric field.

articleTitle: Study on Stem EDS for GESI Atomic Layer Interface Identified and Concentration Quantified
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The Transmission Electron Microscope (TEM) with its high spatial resolution, combines morphology observation, crystal structure identification, and chemical composition analysis functions, enabling direct observations of morphology, interfaces, and crystal defects from the micron to atomic scale. This technology is essential for analyzing the nano-scale GeSi Film and its 2-3 Dumbbell atoms interface distribution in Finfet advanced process to achieve corresponding process optimization. However, traditional Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry (SIMS) is limited to analyzing the GeSi concentration of bare wafer due to its micrometer scanning spot. Atom Probe Tomography (APT) offers great advantages for quantitative analysis of GeSi concentration in devices, but it has a low success rate and high cost due to the necessary Focused Ion Beam (FIB) sample preparation and on-board APT analysis. X-ray Energy Dispersive Spectroscopy (EDS) is generally limited to qualitative and semi-quantitative analysis, making accurate quantitative analysis of GeSi concentration in devices leads to a key challenge in EPI process development. In this study, we focused on developing High-Angle Annular Dark Field (HAADF) imaging technology based on spherical aberration-corrected scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), as well as utilizing EDS and Electron Energy Loss Spectroscopy (EELS) component characterization techniques for ultra-high resolution interface analysis of GeSi films. By optimizing FIB sample preparation methods, combined with EELS Zero Loss monitoring of sample thickness and SIMS calibration of GeSi bare wafer concentrations, EDS can achieve comparable accuracy with SIMS in quantitatively analyzing the GeSi concentration in devices with deviation values less than 1% and maintaining stability across multiple tested data. Currently, a single EDS analysis method can be used for quantitative analysis of GeSi in devices.

articleTitle: Advanced Spectral Sensing Methods for Process Monitoring Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Analytical measurement to determine the quantitative composition of sample mixtures is gaining in importance alongside the widespread measurement of basic physical parameters such as level, temperature or pressure. It is becoming a key factor in the safe operation and control of chemical processes in a wide range of applications. miniaturized analytical systems and spectral sensors based on molecular absorption in the near or mid-infrared range are suitable in many cases to meet specific user requirements such as cost-effectiveness, integrability and reliability. [1]. The paper provides a brief overview of spectral technologies in the near infrared region for chemical process monitoring, in particular on the measurement of liquids. We focus on two measurement systems with different spectral selection principles and performance capabilities. One of the systems is based on the use of Micro Electro Mechanical System (MEMS), the other one uses light emitting diodes for spectral selection. Their design and principles, with respect to the sample implementation, will be described. Furthermore, aspects of calibration development will be pointed out.

articleTitle: A Hardware Accelerator for Sparse Computing Based on NVDLA
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This paper introduces a hardware acceleration architecture based on sparsity and implements it on the foundation of NVDLA. This optimization accelerates computation and reduces dynamic power consumption by actively skipping zero elements in the convolution. The design adopts a sparse compressing method, CSB, and a load balancing algorithm. The design is implemented on the XILINX ZYNQ 7045 FPGA platform, with an operating frequency set at 100MHz. The result achieves a 1.79x acceleration, with power consumption reduced to 91.36% of its pre-optimization value at the cost of only 9.5% increase in area.

articleTitle: Threshold Voltage Mismatch Dependence of SRAM Yield Window Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Statistical SRAM yield Vt (threshold voltage) window analysis has become a growing concern for the requirement of high integration density of SRAM under process variations [1]. SRAM read and write yield window is dominated by median value and local variation of read and write margin. It is found that SRAM array have read and write yield when read and write margin need larger than 6 read and write local variation [2]. In this paper, we investigate the correlation between SRAM VT MM and read and write margin local variation by H-spice simulation. Through the optimization of SRAM device VT MM, read and write margin local variation can be improvement. Therefore, we can predict the optimized SRAM yield Vth window based on the optimized read and write margin local variation and the Vth mismatch.

articleTitle: A Universal Auto Configured Efuse Solution on ADVANTEST V93000 ATE Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: eFuse is widely applied in disposable programmable memory in chip, written into specific data before delivery from factory. With the device scale and complexity increased rapidly, a universal and reliable eFuse solution becomes so important that helps avoid fatal failure. Typical test program usually burns used bit into ‘1’ and keeps unused bit with ‘0’. For those normal system on chip devices, a common and universal configured eFuse solution is necessary for those family devices. Based on these requirements, this paper introduces the relevant analysis, framework design and result implemented on ADVANTEST V93000 ATE platform.

articleTitle: Optimization of Deep Trench Isolation on 0.18μm SOI BCD Technology for Automotive Application
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Deep trench isolation (DTI) is widely used in high voltage BCD technologies in SOI due to its great area shrinkage and excellent isolation capability. X-FAB has utilized the benefits of DTI which enables broad portfolio of highly modular high voltage solution in XT018 [1] [2] and XT011 technology node for automotive applications. The DTI is used for device termination and isolation between adjacent device in circuit to prevent parasitic channel formation, which shown in Fig. 1. As the DTI process integration is rather complex and challenging, the process needs to be well-optimized and robust enough to achieve sustainable manufacturability. This work describes the improvement of defectivity, electrical, yield, as well as reliability performance realized by DTI process optimization.

articleTitle: Improved Performance of PMOS by Optimizing the Epitaxial Morphology
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Since the emergence of the fully depleted silicon on insulator (FDSOI) structure, it has exhibited a wide range of potential applications due to its notable advantages in terms of exceptional radiation resistance and low power consumption. However, owing to the distinctive nature of the FDSOI structure, numerous challenges are encountered during its manufacturing process. We found that the epitaxial morphology at the source and drain of a PMOS device can have an impact on the electrical performance of the device. In this study, we optimized the SiGe epitaxial morphology in PMOS source and drain regions within FDSOI structures by adjusting process parameters such as temperature, effectively resolving issues related to abnormal epitaxial growth. Consequently, significant enhancements were achieved in terms of Ion-Ioff performance while ensuring minimal drain induced barrier lowering (DIBL).

articleTitle: A Novel Approach for Doping Two-Dimensional MOS2 Materials: ZNO Polar Interfacial Charge Transfer Method
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The performance of monolayer Mos2 devices is restricted by low carrier density and contact resistivity. It is crucial to discover a new doping technology to overcome these limitations. In this study, we have devised a novel approach for doping Mos2. By utilizing the ZnO polarity of the different elements interface, Mos2 can be doped with n/p doping. We also constructed a dual-ended device and found that this method indeed increased the intrinsic current at 4.5nm by 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> times.

articleTitle: Solution-Processed Organic CMOS Inverter via Contact Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Organic field-effect transistors (OFETs) have been widely studied, yet realizing complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) integrated circuits still poses significant challenges. Here, we use a single layer of ambipolar polymer organic semiconductor (OSC) to achieve solution-processable organic CMOS inverters by modulating the metal-semiconductor contacts so as to reduce the Schottky barriers for N/P MOS respectively. Ti-contacted (Titanium) N-type OFETs and Au-contacted (gold) P-type OFETs are fabricated on the same substrate. This technology not only presents the advantages of low cost and large-scale integration but also possesses a straightforward processing method, providing a promising solution to the realization of organic CMOS circuits.

articleTitle: An 18.3~42.1GHz Octave Frequency Tuning Class-C Quadcore VCO Achieving 204.5 dBc/Hz FOMT
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This article reports an octave millimeter-wave (mmwave) oscillator in a 28nm CMOS process. Combining class-C operation and mode-switching technology, the proposed VCO achieves an ultra-wide tuning range with low power consumption. Four reconfigurable modes are generated by magnetic and electric coupling. A dynamic bias circuit is utilized to ensure a robust start-up of all four oscillation cores. Based on the post-layout simulations, the VCO exhibits a wide turning range from 18.3 to 42.1GHz and low phase noise from -102.7 to -108.6dBc/Hz at 1MHz frequency offset over the whole operating frequency.
