articleTitle: Nucleation and Growth Study of Al2O3 Film Fabricated Through Atomic Layer Deposition on Pet Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The optical parameters and compactness of ultrathin film on flexible substrates are important for the encapsulation of photoelectric devices. However, guaranteeing optical properties in inorganic films on flexible organic substrates proves challenging due to temperature sensitivity. Here, ultrathin Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> films on Si, glass, and flexible PET substrates are fabricated using atomic layer deposition (ALD). Films on PET displayed infiltration and nucleation during initial growth, while those on glass experienced nucleation delay. Examining plasma pretreatment and post-treatment effects on refractive index and transmittance in ultra-thin Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> films on flexible substrates, O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> plasma-assisted ALD exhibited a high refractive index, excellent uniformity, and robust mechanical flexibility. This makes it a promising choice for encapsulation layers in flexible electronics.

articleTitle: SoC Profile Control for BEOL Tri-Layer Patterning Scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: A tri-layer mask scheme consisting of photoresist (PR), Si-based anti-reflection coating (SiARC) and spin-on-carbon (SOC) is widely used to transfer initial PR pattern to the underneath patterning layer (PL). To perform desired pattern transfer, it is critical to achieve a vertical SOC profile after the SOC etch step. The spacing CD is primarily determined by the selectivity to SiARC during etching of SOC while the profile of SOC requires sidewall passivation from the etch chemistry. However, for most BEOL applications, the use of sulfur-based passivation gases is limited, resulting in weak sidewall and top protection, which poses significant challenges to achieve desired SOC profile. In this work, we propose a solution for SOC profile control for BEOL applications requiring small CD and vertical profiles. In our approach, the SOC etch step consists of recipe A (oxygen based, higher selectivity to SiARC) and recipe B (non-oxygen based, lower selectivity but less lateral etching). This work discusses the strategy for the combination of recipe A and recipe B.

articleTitle: SPAD-Based Line Sensor IC for Chemiluminescence Assays in Microfluidic Channels
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel microchip architecture for a single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD)-based line sensor tailored for in-vitro diagnostic chemiluminescence assays in micro fluidic channels. Our work describes the specific design and optimization aspects of SPADs, including optical active area maximization and dark count rate (DCR) reduction while maintaining a high photon detection probability. The chip architecture features a high -density SP AD sensor array (192 rows) with hot pixel calibration for improved SNR. It supports row-wise pulse counting, adjustable measurement intervals, on-chip SRAM for data storage, ALU with memory-saving bfloat16 encoding, and interfacing via I2C and QSPI.

articleTitle: Interface Treatment of Epitaxial SI FINFET Channel in Replace Metal Gate with Simultaneously Performance Improvement and Leakage Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Channel surface defects are an important factor causing poor device interface characteristics and deterioration of sub-threshold characteristics. In order to reduce the interface trap density (Dit) of epitaxial silicon FinFET devices and improve device performance, an in-situ steam generation (ISSG) oxidation and diluted hydrofluoric acid (DHF) cleaning method was proposed to repair the damaged channel surface and reduce the interface defect charge (Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">it</inf>) replace metal gate (RMG) module. The thickness of Fin top narrows, and Fin's steepness decreases, after interfacial ISSG oxidation treatment. The electrical results demonstrate that the SS for the NFET with interface treatment are decreased from 74.2 mv/dec to 70.97 mV/dec due to the interface improvement. At the same time, the leakage current reduced from 1.0E-2 μA to 5.67E-4 μA, and the Ion is increased by 16.89% compared with that of conventional FinFET without interface treatment.

articleTitle: A.I. Driven Process Control by Machine Learning Based Virtual Metrology for High Product Mix Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The semiconductor foundry industry faces challenges in managing diverse customer demands and complex manufacturing processes. Variations in the chemical vapor deposition (CVD) process affect transistor parameters and yield. Siemens' Calibre® software with artificial intelligence / machine learning (AI/ML) techniques create a virtual metrology (VM) model that outperforms traditional methods. An advanced process control (APC) system, incorporating design features and real-time data, improves process capability and reduces film thickness variations in high-mix product foundry fabs, as confirmed by control simulations.

articleTitle: Designing and Accelerating Spiking Neural Network Based on High-Level Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to use an advanced spiking neural network algorithm, and accelerate the algorithm with a variety of acceleration methods based on the high-level synthesis platform. Its target is to solve the problem of insufficient performance of the traditional computing platform in real-time electrocardiogram data processing. The experiment shows that the performance is improved significantly, which proves that the proposed method is effective in real-time data processing.

articleTitle: Low Frequency Noise and Hot Carrier Degradation Characteristics on 55nm LP Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The integration of 55-nm radio frequency (RF) and mixed-signal technology on the low power (LP) platform has enabled highly integrated system on chip (SoC) solutions. The RF CMOS technology, known for its high integration and cost-effectiveness, is widely used in RF front-end modules like voltage-controlled oscillators (VCO), power amplifiers (P A), low noise amplifiers (LNA), and switches. Hot carrier injection (HCI) poses a reliability challenge in analog/RF circuit design on the 55nm LP platform. This paper presents an assessment of HCI reliability in two groups of thick gate oxide NIO FETs with different 10 LDD implant conditions. By optimizing the 10 LDD implant, the HCI lifetime is shown to be 3.5 times higher with a lighter arsenic dose (LDD-) compared to a higher dose (LDD+). Low frequency noise is another critical parameter for RF and mixed-signal applications, particularly in the Internet of Things (IoT) field. The low frequency noise upconverted to phase noise of VCO can degrade the performance of RF front-end chips. In this paper, hot carrier degradation and low frequency noise characteristics are investigated for NIO FETs. The coupling results between HCI and low frequency noise are also investigated, contributing to the advancement of RF and mixed-signal platforms.

articleTitle: A Novel Gan-Based Data Augmentation Algorithm for Semiconductor Defect Inspection
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: A deep learning solution is proposed for the problem of object inspection in semiconductor images. Supervised learning method approaches require large annotated semiconductor datasets, which are often difficult to obtain. Therefore, we develop a new deep convolutional generative adversarial network (DCGAN)) to generate simulated data. Real image data and generated image data are used to train the residual network (ResNet) defect inspection network. Compared to training with the original dataset, using the synthetic dataset resulted in a 3.12% improvement in the accuracy of local defect detection. The total defect inspection accuracy also improves from 93.75% to 95.31%.

articleTitle: STI Gap-Filling Performance Improvement by the Process Integration Optimization in the 4XNM ETOX NOR Flash
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The gap-fill performance of shallow trench isolation (STI) plays an important role in the cell size shrink of ETOX Nor flash. In this work, we optimize the SIN pullback and high-density plasma (HDP) process to improve STI gap-fill, and the gap-fill performances are investigated by the wafer accept test (WAT) and chip probe (CP). And the void-free gap-fill and the comparable WAT/CP performance are achieved by the process integration of SIN pullback with suitable HPO dosage and the optimized Dep-Etch-Dep cycle of HDP.

articleTitle: Predicting Material Removal Rate in Chemical Mechanical Polishing (CMP) Using Explainable Machine Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Chemical Mechanical Polishing (CMP) is a crucial process in integrated circuit manufacturing. To determine the material removal rate in this process, three different models were employed for learning and prediction. Among them, the XGBoost (eXtreme Gradient Boosting) algorithm yielded the best performance, achieving an R-squared value of 0.87. Using SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) in conjunction with the XGBoost model, an assessment of feature importance was conducted. Utilizing these identified features as inputs for training, the R-squared value improved to 0.89 under the XGBoost algorithm. These findings were summarized, with a detail discussion feature importance based on the physical and chemical processes associated with CMP.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Study to Obtain an Optimal Processing Pulsed Frequency on Reactive Pulsed DC Sputtering of Aluminum Nitride Films
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The goal of this study was to investigate how changing the pulsed frequency affects the deposition process and correlates with AlN film properties. The resulting films were then characterized in terms of their crystallinity, microstructure, and surface roughness to identify any correlations with the pulsed frequency. This approach was used to determine the optimal pulsed conditions for film deposition. Each dataset spans the wavelength range of 190nm to 850nm, comprising 1,900 features. Following data collection, we employed traditional ensemble learning methods (Random Forest), tree-based gradient boosting (Categorical Boosting), and the improved gradient-boosted algorithm (Histogram Gradient Boosting), for predicting the quality of thin films. This analysis aimed to clarify which method excels in handling semiconductor process OES data to obtain an optimal processing pulsed frequency on reactive pulsed DC sputtering of aluminum nitride films.

articleTitle: Effective Resistance Estimation for Large Circuits Using Random Walk Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: We propose a method for estimating the effective resistance of large circuits using a random walk algorithm. In this method, a particle randomly hops among circuit nodes based on the circuit's topology, and the hopping probabilities are determined accordingly. We introduce two effective resistance estimation (ERE) algorithms for different scenarios: ERE between any two nodes and ERE between all nodes and a reference node. To reduce the statistical error of ERE, we repeat the random walk processes multiple times. Additionally, we compare the results obtained from this method with those obtained from a rigid solving method to evaluate its effectiveness.

articleTitle: A Novel DES Encryption Circuit Based on RRAM XOR Gates
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, an XOR logic gate circuit based on the resistive random-access memory (RRAM) is developed, and the conventional complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) XOR gates in Date Encryption Standard (DES) encryption circuitry are replaced with RRAM XOR gates. This work is the first to apply the RRAM to cryptographic circuits, showcasing the feasibility of leveraging novel non-volatile memories (NVMs) to realize data encryption. Relative to conventional encryption circuit, the proposed circuitry has a significant advantage in terms of hardware circuit area, achieving an impressive reduction of over 11.43%.

articleTitle: Comparison of Simulation and Test Results of Multi-Type Ring Oscillators on Advanced Process Nodes
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, we present the simulation and test result of various ring oscillators(ROs) based on state-of-the-art process node(FinFET technology). We designed five basic structures, based on which 90 kinds of ROs with different dirving strengths and devices types were generated. Under the differrnt conditions of voltage, we compared the EVB&ATE test data and SPICE simulation data of these ROs, and analyzed the impact of various factors on mismatch, which digitally confirms the feasibility of using path delay(PD) sensor like RO to monitor process variation and continuously focuses on yield improvement. Meanwhile, speed performance of ROs composed of gate-all-around(GAA)FETs are also simulated using TCAD intends to investgate the influences of process parameters, as nanosheets .

articleTitle: Polyimides for Power Device Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: High voltage power semiconductor devices are required for such as automobiles, trains, and high-voltage power transmission. Those high voltage power devices usually are coated with polyimide which is used to suppress leakage at interface of high voltage power device. The polyimide is required to protect from ionic contamination to the power device interface. We have designed a polyimide precursor structure with high light transparency, alkaline solubility and high thermal stability after cure. A novel negative-tone photo-definable polyimide was formulated with cross linking reagent that can easily decompose during cure and high efficiency photo-initiator. Our novel Negative photo sensitive polyimide (PSPI-1) has a patternable capability up to 16 μm thickness on silicon wafer with 350 μmJ/cm2 exposure dose. Photo patternability of PSPI-1 is better than that of the conventional polyimide. The cured film showed excellent properties as follows: 310 °C glass transition temperature (Tg), 500 °C 5% weight loss temperature, 40% elongation, no short observation during bias-HAST (130 °C. 96%, 100hr, 100V 15/30 °m line & space) and good adhesion to Si and Cu substrates. These results indicated a possibility for this novel PSPI-1 to be applicable for passivating power semiconductor.

articleTitle: A Novel Thin Film Deposition Method by IBD for Asymmetrical Patterns
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Blazed gratings have excellent optical properties because they transmit the majority of the energy of the incident beam to a non-zero diffraction order, which facilitates spectral analysis and detection. They have a wide application in AR/VR and are fabricated by research institutes, IDMs and foundries. To further improve or optimize the reflectivity and the transmissivity, coating for blazed or anti-blazed face by different materials is important. For traditional deposition method, it is impossible to deposit different materials for each sidewall. The directional deposition of ion beam deposition (IBD) can achieve the deposition at a specific position. We make it possible to deposit various materials for each sidewall of blazed gratings. Leuven Instruments can provide a unique asymmetrical deposition method to help our customers achieve flexible deposition needs.

articleTitle: Effect of Process Parameters on Microstructure and Properties of ITO Films by Pulsed Magnetron Sputtering
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Indium tin oxide (ITO) films are widely used in many fields such as flat panel display, solar cell, etc. In this study, DC and pulsed DC magnetron sputtering were used to deposit ITO on silicon substrates. The microstructure and properties of ITO films were studied at different deposition temperatures. Transmission electron microscope (TEM) and X-ray diffractometer (XRD) were used to investigate the changes in the microstructure of ITO films, while atomic force microscope (AFM) and scanning electron microscope (SEM) were used to characterize surface morphology and roughness. At the same time, four-point probe method explores the effects of structural change on the sheet resistance of ITO. In addition, ITO was deposited on the glass substrate to investigate the effects of changing deposition conditions on ITO transmittance.

articleTitle: A Modularized Thermal Test Chip Design and Verification
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: With the development of system on chip, the power distribution in the chip becomes more complicated. Clock frequency increasing and high speed signal rate multiplication make certain local power to be much more higher compared to the average power in the chip. The evaluation and testing of thermal solution becomes more challenge due to complex power distribution in chip. To simply the evaluation the thermal performance of chip, a thermal test chip(TTC) is developed, in which the power distribution is controllable and large numbers of temperature sensors is available, to reproduce the real chip power distribution and temperature map. In this paper, the design of modularized thermal test chip is illustrated firstly, in which there is a heater and a resistance temperature detective sensor using BEOL serpentine metal resistance. The module size is about 1mm square. Heater and sensor are designed with Kelvin-connection for accurately measurement. Secondly, the thermal test chip is verified by resistance measurement and the statistics results indicate resistance of heater is within ±10%. RTD sensor has high linearity after calibration. And an uniform power test is conducted, which the temperate difference between test and simulation is within ±1°C. Thirdly, the method using TTC to reproduce a real chip power map is introduced. From the simulation results we can find the modularized TTC can obtain an almost the same temperature map compared to real chip, by adjusting the power distribution of heater.

articleTitle: AL2O3/ALOX Memristor with Nearly Ideal Synaptic Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This work demonstrates that a memristor based on bilayer oxides with a stack structure of Pt/Ti/Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/AlO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</inf>/Ti/Pt can perform the nearly ideal synaptic characteristics for energy-efficient neuromorphic computing. The engineered oxygen content promotes the formation of the uniform oxygen vacancy distribution, leading to steadily widening conductive filaments rather than abruptly forming. This provides an effective way to meet the requirement of gradually setting/resetting of synapses, which can achieve multilevel states of conductance and long-term potentiation/depression (LTP/LTD). Training on the MNIST machine-learning dataset demonstrates that this memristor exhibits online learning accuracy exceeding 80%.

articleTitle: Research on Integrated Trench Etching for Trench-Type Power MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In the manufacturing process of trench-type metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor (MOSFET), trench etching is a crucial step that directly influences subsequent processes such as gate oxidation, polysilicon deposition, and the final device performance. This research elucidates the process challenges encountered during the development of the integrated trench etching process, including tapered trench morphology, microtrenches, incomplete resist stripping, and insufficient etch selectivity. Through adjustments to process parameters such as pressure, power, gas composition, and gas ratios, the study successfully addressed the challenges. The insights from this research may provide inspiration for the improvement of trench etching steps in other power devices.

articleTitle: Verification of 400 GbE on an FPGA Platform with Optical Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: With the increasing processing data traffic of big data, 5G networks, 8K video and other applications, the existing 100 Gb/s transmission system is no longer sufficient. This paper proposes a 400 Gb/s Ethernet (400 GbE) verification platform based on FPGA (Field-Programmable Gate Array), including TRX (transceiver) PMA (Physical Medium Attachment), 400 Gb/s QSFP-DD (Quad Small Form-factor Pluggable Double Density) optical modules and optical fibers, 8-lane QSFP-DD MCB (Module Compliance Board), which is used for loopback and outgoing signals to facilitate testing. The PAM-4 (Pulse-Amplitude Modulation 4-Level) is adopted, and the TRX PMA terminal has 8×53.125 Gb/s electrical signals, which will be converted into 4×106.25 Gb/s optical signals through the optical modules. The feasibility of this verification platform has been demonstrated by measuring the signal eye height and eye width and monitoring the error rate of the loopback link, laying the foundation for future research on implementing 400 Gb/s SmartNIC (Network Interface Card) based on FPGA, integrating PCIe (Peripheral Component Interconnect Express) 6.0 and CXL (Compute Express Link) 3.0 technologies.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation on the Back-Gate Modulation of Extra-Thin Body Pmosfets
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The back-gate modulation of body silicon-on-insulator (SOI) pMOSFETs with different channel thicknesses is systematically investigated by experiments and simulations. It is found that the carrier density and distribution would be hardly affected by the back-gate voltage for the 2-nm-thick extra-thin body (ETB) SOI pMOSFET, which is due to the strong surface roughness scattering simultaneously from the front and back gate interface. In this case, both front and back gate stacks with high-quality interfaces are crucial for the carrier transport properties in the ETB SOI pMOSFET.

articleTitle: A Fully Automated VPD System for Noble Metal Control During CIS Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Metallic contamination has long been reported as a source of defects for most semiconductor devices, and its impacts on complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) image sensors (CISs) are especially detrimental. These contaminants could be introduced during the CIS fabrication, such as ion implantation process [1]–[2]. Wafer surface concentration of certain noble metals, including Au, Ag, and Pt, needs to be controlled to no more than 0.05 to 0.2 ppt [6]. Conventional methods of metal trace analysis involve chemically collecting these elements into a scanning solution, and analyzing the diluted scanning solution by inductively coupled plasma mass spectroscopy (ICP-MS). However, detecting the concentration of noble metals on wafer surface has been particularly challenging, due to their low solubility in scanning solutions. In this paper, the authors proposed a method to effectively collect the noble metals, especially silver and gold, with an aqua regia (AR) based scanning solution to increase the collection efficiency (CE). Combined with a vapor phase decomposition (VPD) treatment of the wafer surface, and an integrated ICP-MS analysis, our fully automated method of AR based noble metal collection is of great importance to control the noble metal contamination for CIS manufacturing.

articleTitle: Runtime Configurable Approximate Computing System for Simulated Annealing Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a runtime configurable approximate computing (RCAC) system for simulated annealing (SA) algorithm. The RCAC system integrates a configurable approximate hardware to calculate the cost function and a lightweight quality estimator, which provides valuable insights into the SA algorithm's effectiveness by estimating the acceptance rate of each iteration. By utilizing the acceptance rate, the system dynamically configures the operational mode of the approximate hardware, making a good trade-off between solution quality and computational efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate a 7.6% runtime improvement compared to traditional RCAC methods on SA algorithms with a quality loss of less than 2% in final solutions.

articleTitle: Study on Chemical-Mechanical Synergies in Polishing of Ruthenium
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Ruthenium (Ru) is widely used in the manufacturing of integrated circuits due to its excellent properties such as low electrical resistivity and good step coverage. The Chemical Mechanical Polishing (CMP) of Ru has been extensively researched, with emphasis on the development of slurry to improve the material removal rate of Ru. The chemical-mechanical synergistic material removal mechanisms of Ru have not received in-depth investigation. To address this gap, CMP of polycrystalline Ru was carried out with polishing pads of different elastic modulus and slurries containing varying oxidizer concentrations. The experimental results demonstrated significant differences in grain boundary step heights under different polishing conditions. This paper suggests that the observed variations in grain boundary step heights during Ru polishing are the result of the interplay between oxide layer thickness (chemical action) and particle penetration depth (mechanical action). Thus, by elucidating the differences in experimental results, this paper reveals the material removal mechanisms associated with the chemical-mechanical synergy in Ru polishing.

articleTitle: Copper Diffusion Improvement by Optimizing TaN and Integration in Power Device
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Copper (Cu) interconnect has been widely used for large scale integrated circuits in logic process technology nodes of 90 nm and beyond. Tantalum nitride (TaN) as the barrier film plays a significant role in device reliability. TaN film prevents Cu diffusion into the Al bond-pad layer and the dielectric layer which will lead to voids in top metal Cu as well as circuit leakage increase that impacts product yield and reliability. Therefore, it is very important to optimize TaN film in back-end of line (BEoL) integration. In this study, TaN film's barrier ability to prevent Cu diffusion was investigated. These results indicate that Cu diffusion can be improved by tuning TaN film barrier properties as well as optimizing process integration flow.

articleTitle: Universal Process Migration Solution of MAGICAL for Analog IC Layout Automation
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Analog IC layout automation has been a hot topic in the field in recent years[1]. An open-source software MAGICAL developed by the University of Texas team is one of the most effective means to achieve this goal[2]. However, so far MAGICAL is only able to support one process library currently, i.e., TSMC 40nm, and this imposes limitations of its practical application. This work proposes a solution for the technology migration of MAGICAL, and this greatly broadens its application scenarios. Firstly, the MAGICAL's device generator is rewritten to take in the general design rule information of different technology nodes. Second, the parameters of a given technology's tech file are extracted by customerized Parameter Extractor. Finally, the extracted parameters are set into the device generator of MAGICAL as well as the LEF file used for routing. As demonstrations, layouts of multiple circuits such as inverter, Foleded Cascode, Nbooster and Pbooster are generated sucessfully using this new flow at different technology nodesincluding but not limited to TSMC 65nm and TSMC 130nm. In addition, all GDS files generated with this method are DRC-clean and LVS-clean. This work paves the way for MAGICAL to be used in design automation at various technology nodes.

articleTitle: Decoupling Capacitor Optimization for 2.5D-ICs With Deep Reinforcement Learning Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a deep reinforcement learning-based design method that provides decoupling capacitor (decap) arrangement approaches on 2.5D integrated circuit (2.5D-IC) designs. The proposed method provides a guideline of decap design to reduce the influence of simultaneous switch noise (SSN). We consider the multi-chiplet design, the capacitors placement constraint, and cost of capacitors when optimizing the power delivery network (PDN) impedance. This method achieves 24% less capacitor requirement when compared to the traditional algorithm.

articleTitle: New Generation Test Framework Solution for Complicated Multi-Die Chip on ATE
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: With the development of ChipLet technique in the semiconductor industry, more and more chips are consist of multi dies and each die is designed by many different kinds of analog IP or complicated high-speed interface PHY, which has been facing much more serious challenges (such as the efficiency of complicated pattern iteration, the strict control of bench correlation condition, the promotion of test coverage, etc). Under this background, this paper will provide a new generation test solution for the above challenges of complicated Multi-Die chip and a common program framework on ATE (Auto Test Equipment) has been implement to support the solution.

articleTitle: Novel Memtransistor-Based Lif Neuron with Tunable Ionic Dynamics for Spiking Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: To realize energy-efficient intelligent systems for spiking neural networks, we propose a novel compact artificial neuron based on ion-modulated memtransistors, which can realize the leaky, integrate-and-fire (LIF) functions by utilizing the ionic dynamics. Through the spontaneous decay dynamics of ions, the proposed neurons can avoid external capacitors or any other reset circuits. Moreover, we explore the influences of neuron firing under different stimulation parameters and tunable decay time constants under different base voltages; by adding this extra freedom of modulation, the network performances can be boosted.

articleTitle: A Study of High Aspect Ratio Si Trench in Cycle Mode Etching with Mask no Loss
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Accurate and strict etching processes are the development requirements for the continuous integration of semiconductor devices. In this paper, we based on CH3F/Ar dep and implemented it to the plasma etching process of dep-etch cycle, achieving a high aspect ratio and depth controllable Si trench etching with mask no-loss.

articleTitle: Cu Post CMP Cleaner Development Utilizing AI System
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: CMP (Chemical Mechanical Polishing) is a process that is widely used in the manufacturing of semiconductors, particularly for the BEOL (Back End Of Line) process which involves multi-level interconnections. Copper (Cu) is commonly used as the wiring metal in the BEOL process. Cu CMP plays a crucial role in achieving the necessary planarization of the BEOL layer for effective alignment of multiple layers. In recent times, Cu CMP has gained significance in 3D integration schemes such as hybrid bonding and TSV (Through Silicon Via). For the Cu slurry in the CMP process, 1H-Benzotriazole (BTA) is known to be an effective Cu corrosion inhibitor that helps in achieving better planarization. However, the use of BTA is often associated with the formation of organic residue in the CMP process. Therefore, a specialized chemical for post CMP (pCMP) cleaning is required to remove any residue of BTA. On this occasion, we conducted a special exploration of additives using an AI system to achieve selective removal of BTA specifically from Cu surfaces. The system classified a large number of parameters and identified specific parameters for BTA removal and Cu compatibility. Following regression analysis using these parameters, we observed a strong correlation with actual experimental results. In conclusion, our Cu pCMP cleaner, which includes a special additive designed by the AI system, exhibited commendable cleaning performance.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Sram Read and Write Noise Margin by Device Performance Adjustment
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The continuous shrinking of device size and the lower power-supplied voltage bring challenges to SRAM reading and writing stability. Compared with some methods of improving read and write stability by losing area, speed, or power consumption. Improving the standard deviation cannot only increase read and write windows but also does not reduce the device itself performance. This paper tried to reduce the reading and writing margin variation by adjusting the lightly doped drain (LDD) of NMOS. An appropriate LDD dosage can simultaneously make the read and write window 2 sigma larger than BSL in traditional 6T SRAM.

articleTitle: Modeling of Endurance Degradation of Anti-Ferroelectric HF1-xZRxO2 Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The anti-ferroelectric HfZrO oxide has drawn attention due to its non-volatile characteristics (with a build-in bias) and high dielectric constant which is very important for DRAM applications. Therefore, understanding the evolution of P-V curves during the endurance cycling becomes crucial for evaluating the reliability behaviors of anti - ferroelectric HfZrO capacitors. In this work, we developed an endurance degradation model of anti-ferroelectric HfZrO capacitors. The proposed degradation model demonstrates excellent prediction capability for P-V curve evolution during the endurance cycling with different stress amplitudes.

articleTitle: The Optimization of the Specific On-Resistance of the Vdmos on the Integrated Platform of Vdmos and Ldmos
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: As is known to all, the operation modes of vertical double-diffused MOS (VDMOS) and lateral double-diffused MOS (LDMOS) are completely different, so retaining performance of the VDMOS will be difficult to deal with the new platform due to variant working modes. A way of optimizing the key performance, specific on-resistance (Rsp) of the vertical double-diffused MOS (VDMOS) on the integrated platform is proposed in this letter. The Rsp of VDMOS is optimized by implanting impurity and long thermal process which is engaged in the platform. The T-CAD simulation and experiments results indicate that the performance of VDMOS is retained successfully.

articleTitle: Challenges of Semiconductor Micro Via Fabrication Technology for 3D Chiplet Interconnect
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Chiplet integration technology, which has the potential to scalable expand capabilities by integrating many IC chips with different manufacturing processes, structures, and functions while maintaining the data transfer bandwidth between IC chips, is attracting attention as a promising method to solve the problems such as slowdown of Moore's law and the von Neumann bottleneck. Die-to-die bridge structures that connect dies via locally placed bridge chips with high-density interconnects is expected for scalable chiplet integration. In this paper, we propose plasma etching technologies to realize novel die-to-die bridge architecture called “Pillar-Suspended Bridge (PSB)”, and new through-silicon via etching technologies for 3D-IC integration, as well.

articleTitle: A Study on Floating Gate Profile Control and Reliability Improvement in Planar 1XNM Nand Flash
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: As the critical feature size shrinkage on planar 2D NAND flash, conventional N-type poly silicon using as floating gate cannot meet the requirement for higher cycling performance. Electric trap in tunnel oxide during cycling further made cycling window margin. Using P-type poly silicon to replace N-type poly silicon showed great benefit for reliability improvement, because hole-injection features of P-type poly silicon floating gate can minimize Vth shift. However, continuous design pitch shrinkage and boron-dopants in P-type poly silicon both made gate poly etching process more challenging. In this work, profile control and selectivity optimization for poly gate etching are studied by adjusting each etching step with variable gas ratio, source/bias power ratio and power delivery methods. As a result, better floating gate profile without silicon oxide fence and silicon pitting was achieved, and reliability performance showed significant improvement.

articleTitle: A Method for Predicting the Film Thickness of IC Deposited Films Based on FCBF-CATBOOST
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This article presents a novel method for predicting film thickness of IC deposited films. The study uses the category boosting (CatBoost) to predict film deposition thickness, employs the Fast Correlation-Based Filter (FCBF) for data cleaning of the relevant process parameters, feature extraction, and uses grid search and cross-validation for hyperparameter optimization. Through experiments using regression metrics such as R-Squared and Mean Square Error, FCBF-CatBoost demonstrates higher prediction accuracy compared to algorithms like support vector machine (SVM), XGBoost and random forest (RF).

articleTitle: Sidewall Kink Elimination of Slanted Gratings Utilizing a Twice-Etching Method
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The slanted grating is crucial to cutting -edge disciplines like spectroscopy, augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), etc. The kink of the slanted grating sidewall will affect the diffraction efficiency of the optical waveguide couplers utilized in AR devices. In the fabrication of slanted gratings in reactive ion beam etching (RIBE), a kinky sidewall is difficult to avoid. A twice-etching method is proposed to resolve this issue. Through the combination of two processes, a better slanted grating morphology without kinky sidewall is achieved. This work has good guiding significance for the fabrication of slanted gratings.

articleTitle: A 106TOPS/W SRAM Compute-in-Memory Macro in 28NM With Reconfigurable Bitwise Operation for AI
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This paper proposes a 64kb SRAM-based full-precision reconfigurable Compute-In-Memory (CIM) architecture in a 28nm technology. Both MAC and basic Boolean operation units are integrated within the CIM macro, which allows the system to adapt to different computational tasks. The Adder tree, a critical building block in CIM, is optimized by utilizing a simplified 14-T based full adder. This optimization leads to improvements in energy efficiency and savings in area. The simulation results demonstrate the performance of the proposed CIM macro, achieving a 106 TOPS/W energy efficiency at a 0.9V power supply. The total area is around 0.5mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A Novel Method to Improve Sidewall Protection by Adopting Nested Bosch Process
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: With the continuously shrinking of the critical dimension of CMOS, the traditional Moore's Law start to slow down, three-dimensional integrated circuits from the perspective chip packaging solutions have attracted great research attentions. Among the advanced etch structures adopted in 3-D chip package, one of the most important structures is the Through-Si-Via (TSV). In this paper, the etching process of TSV, which has greatly increased the sidewall protection strength during the etching process, is studied to enhance the anisotropy of etching, improve the process limit, increase the process window, and process stability.

articleTitle: Inverse Lithography with Adaptive Mask Complexity
publicationTitle: 2024 Conference of Science and Technology for Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Mask complexity is becoming a critical issue for advanced semiconductor nodes both in optical proximity correction (OPC) and post OPC manufacturing flows, especially when curvilinear features are introduced with inverse lithography technology (ILT) for pattern fidelity improvement. In this paper, we address the mask complexity by adaptively incorporating constant width sub-resolution assist features (SRAFs) into the level-set based inverse lithography. We first extract the SRAFs up to the 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> order with respect to the distance to the main features from a continuous transmission mask (CTM) and distance maps of the features skeleton are constructed. Mask complexity is regulated by applying constant width to the selected orders of SRAF features while the main features and the SARFs with other orders are optimized as freeform pixels. Simulation results show comparable pattern fidelity performance in terms of pattern error (PE) with adaptive constant width SRAF selection, and also mask complexity is reduced because constant width SRAFs, for which curvature and width mask rules are implicitly complied, can be manufactured by less circular shots.
